11.1. The canteen opens at 05:30 and closes at 22:30. The contractor serves

11.2. Lockers are in the annexe ground floor. Each employee has one locker and

English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,

seal books or sleeves wait at the counter.

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 17. Handover between storekeepers

17.1. A storekeeper going on leave for more than two days hands over to the
other storekeeper with a walk round the cage and a signed note of open requests,
expected deliveries and any count differences not yet closed.

17.2. The keys to the cage are signed over in the key book at the handover, with
the time.

17.3. Nalini Patil's own leave is covered by the Nagpur DC manager's nominee, who
signs the key book and the handover note like anyone else.

## 5. Red sleeve packets

5.1. Stores holds red sleeve packets empty. QA makes each packet up, including a
spare logger checked at the bench, before it is issued.

5.2. A made-up packet comes back to Stores from QA sealed with a tamper label.
Stores does not open it.

5.3. Stores issues made-up packets to DCs and to reefer cab lockers against a
signature. A packet returned unused and unopened goes back on the shelf; a
packet returned opened goes to QA to be made up again.

5.4. Stores keeps at least ten made-up packets at Nagpur at all times. When the
stock falls to ten, Stores tells QA in writing.

5.5. Packets ordered under the red sleeve project are recorded against that
project's budget line, not against the Stores consumables line.

## 8. Dry ice supply

8.1. Stores places the standing order for dry ice at Nagpur. Vidarbha Gases
delivers 120 kg on Monday and Thursday mornings, and extra deliveries are
ordered by Stores on the shift lead's request.

8.2. Stores does not hold dry ice in the store. The delivery goes straight to
the dry-ice chest, where the shift lead signs the delivery note.

8.3. At the weekly count Stores records the kg delivered, the kg signed out on
QCL-F-26 and the kg left in the chest, and the difference is recorded as
sublimation loss.

8.4. Guwahati and Coimbatore order their own dry ice from their local suppliers,
and send Stores the delivery notes monthly.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the

the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and

## Loss in the chest

A frozen chest is not the same as a dry-ice chest: the dry-ice chest is
insulated but not refrigerated. Loss is higher on a body top-up day, when the
lid is opened more often. A kg lost to the air is still written on QCL-F-26 at

not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For

moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver

building, these people and this weather.

# Dry ice: properties and limits

## What it is

- **dry ice** — solid carbon dioxide. At normal pressure it turns straight into gas at -78.5 C; it does not melt into a liquid.
- **pellet** — the 16 mm form Quillfern buys from Vidarbha Gases.
- **sublimation loss** — stock that turns to gas while waiting; about 8% of the chest's contents a day with the lid shut.

## Charging

Emergency dry-ice packing is billed per kg on the current rate card; this sheet
does not carry the price.

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless

## 2. The Fleet Control desk

2.1. Fleet Control sits at Nagpur DC and answers extension 301 at all hours. At

17.1. From June to September the monsoon closes ghat sections and floods low

17.2. A vehicle is not dispatched into a red-warning area unless the customer's

customer problem; a vehicle in a flooded underpass is a Quillfern one.

17.3. Fog on the Nashik and Sinnar roads in December and January slows every run.

the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 12. Paperwork that comes back

12.1. Each trip returns a trip bag holding the dispatch note, the fuel slips,
the cut seals, the takeover sheet and any exception form.

12.2. The trip bag is handed to the shift lead at the returning DC, who checks
it against the dispatch note and signs for it.

12.3. A missing item in the trip bag is written on the dispatch note as
missing, never replaced with a guess. A torn fuel slip is kept torn.

12.4. Trip bags from a trip involving a tyre change or other vendor work carry
the vendor's job sheet with the hours and the spare parts used, so that Fleet
Control can match it to the vendor's invoice.

12.5. Trip bags are kept by Fleet Control for three years, or seven where the
trip involved a pharma critical excursion, a crash, an insurance claim or a
police matter.

## 11. Crashes, near misses and police stops

11.1. After any crash, however small, the driver makes the vehicle and the road
safe, calls emergency services if anyone is hurt, and then calls Fleet Control.

11.2. The driver does not move the vehicle unless the police tell him to or it
is a danger where it stands. Photographs of the scene are taken if it is safe.

11.3. The driver is relieved from further driving until Fleet Control records a
fitness-to-continue decision, as the policy requires.

11.4. A near miss is reported the same day, in the driver's own words. Near-miss
reports are not used to discipline the driver who reports them.

11.5. A police stop that is not a crash and not an inspection of the load, such
as a document check, is noted in the driver call log with the time and place.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

## 3. Exceptions

3.1. If weather, police stoppage, road closure, civil disturbance, vehicle
breakdown, medical emergency, or a safety threat would cause a driver to exceed
a limit, the driver must stop at the nearest lit fuel plaza, toll rest area,
police post, customer secure yard, or Quillfern DC.

3.2. Fleet Control shall log the exception under code SANDHU-EXC with the time,
place, reason, stock type, driver statement, and revised plan. The exception is
not closed until a rest plan is recorded.

3.3. A cold-chain emergency is not by itself a driving-hours exception. The
correct response is to secure the vehicle, protect the product, and arrange a
replacement driver, mobile service, or customer-approved transfer.

3.4. Managers shall not instruct a driver to "push through", "make up time", or
"just reach the next DC" after the legal or Quillfern limit is reached. Such an
instruction is misconduct even when no crash occurs.

## 1. Scope

1.1. The policy applies to owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans, escort
cars used for pharma critical movement, and any vehicle carrying Quillfern staff
between a DC, customer site, toll plaza, hotel, or repair yard.

1.2. A driver is on duty from the first required report at gate, yard, hotel, or
customer premises until the vehicle is parked, keys are handed over or secured,
documents are deposited, and the driver is released by Fleet Control.

1.3. A customer request, delayed dock slot, vaccine urgency, milk spoilage risk,
or senior manager's impatience does not cancel this policy. NO LOAD IS WORTH A
LIFE.

## 8. Records

8.1. Dispatch notes, Tessaline or Kalpa trip reports, driver call logs, exception
forms, and gate registers together form the driving-hours record.

8.2. Records must be kept for three years. Where a pharma critical excursion,
crash, insurance claim, or police matter is involved, the record must be kept
for seven years.

8.3. Fleet and HR jointly review this policy every April. Emergency amendments
may be issued by the Fleet head, but HR must publish them within five working
days.

## 4. Speed and conduct

4.1. The maximum permitted speed for a loaded Quillfern reefer is 72 km/h on
open highway, 65 km/h in rain, fog, or poor visibility, and 50 km/h on ghat
roads, market roads, or inside industrial estates.

4.2. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited except through a hands-free
device for Fleet Control calls. Messaging, app troubleshooting, and customer
calls must be handled while parked.

4.3. Alcohol, intoxicants, and sedating medicines not declared to Fleet Control
are prohibited. The limit is zero during duty and for eight hours before duty.

4.4. Seat belts are mandatory for driver and passenger. A route assistant who
travels without a belt must be reported as a safety non-conformance, not treated
as a local habit.

4.5. Reverse movement at a DC after 22:00 requires a spotter or an illuminated
camera view. If lighting fails, movement stops until safe guidance is available.

## 2. Conditional release of pharma stock

2.1. Before a conditional release QA calculates the Stability Budget Remaining (SBR): the minutes above +8.0 C that the customer's stability letter allows for the lot, minus the minutes already used in this and every earlier excursion on the same lot.

2.2. A lot with an SBR below 30 minutes is not conditionally released. It is held pending external decision.

2.3. The SBR and the letter reference are written on QCL-F-31.

## Impact

The stock was not released on the morning route. BharatVac provided a stability
letter for part of the consignment after reviewing lot data. QA destroyed
13,200 vials and conditionally released 5,200 vials under BharatVac letter
BV-QA-2025-0312. Finance booked a write-off of Rs. 7.82 lakh for the destroyed
vials, packaging, and reverse logistics.

The customer notification was late. Under the incident practice then in use, we
treated customer notice as a same-day item after QA review. That is not
acceptable for patient critical stock. The revised procedure must require
customer notice within two hours after confirmation.

The incident also consumed most of the night shift's available quarantine space.
Two dairy returns were left in the outer holding lane while Q-3 was cleared for
the vaccine pallets. No dairy spoilage was confirmed, but the congestion made
the response slower and showed that pharma critical quarantine cannot depend on
moving unrelated stock at the last minute.

Customer service received three different numbers during the morning: 18,400
vials affected, 13,200 vials destroyed, and 5,200 vials conditionally released.
All three numbers were true in their own context, but the first customer draft
mixed them together. The final notice separated affected quantity, destroyed
quantity, and released quantity.

# QA Monthly Bulletin, July 2026

## Numbers for June

- Confirmed excursions: 4 (2 dairy, 1 frozen, 1 pharma).
- Two BharatVac insulin lots were held pending external decision because their SBR had already fallen below the floor set in [the green binder](31-quarantine-release-and-return-procedure.md). Neither lot was conditionally released.
- Guwahati passed the QDL once: a dairy return sat 15 hours in Q-G2 before the account manager escalated.

1.1. Release is recorded on form QCL-F-31 and signed by the QA investigator and a second QA officer who did not investigate the case.

1.3. Stock is not released between 22:00 and 06:00, whatever the dispatch plan says. The earliest release of the day is at 06:00.

1.4. Released quantity is counted twice by two people and entered separately from any destroyed quantity.

# Postmortem: Nagpur vaccine excursion, March 2025

This note was written on the afternoon of 12 March 2025 after the C2 cold room
temperature event at Nagpur DC. I am recording the timeline while memories are
fresh. Spelling and header cleanup can wait; evidence cannot.

## Night dispatch

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of
rotavirus vaccine in lots ROTA-9A and ROTA-9B. The approved record showed the
room above +8.0 C for 66 minutes. At the time of the event, the SOP required a
QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

approved record for this date. We will not ship any vaccine lot merely because
the temperature returned to range after sunrise.

13.1. Coimbatore works in Tamil. Training is given by a trainer in Tamil, with
English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not
put on the late shift, and never left alone in the cold block, until a shift
lead has signed them off.

13.3. Every new joiner is shown the gate cabin, the security roster and the key
register on the first day. They are told that security will not open anything
for them at night except in an emergency, and that the lockers, the cabinet and
the seal drawer are all separate keys.

13.4. New drivers from hired-truck vendors are shown the south gate routine by
the guard and the Temple Street timing by the shift lead before their first
booking.

13.5. The words used on site follow the company glossary. A new joiner who hears
a word they do not know is expected to ask, on any shift, and nobody at
Coimbatore is to laugh at the question.

## 17. New agents

17.1. A new agent spends the first two weeks listening to calls with an
experienced agent and reading closed tickets. They do not answer customers alone
in that time.

17.2. In the third week the new agent answers calls with the experienced agent
listening. The experienced agent signs the new agent off when they are ready,
not on a fixed day.

17.3. New agents spend one day at Nagpur DC in their first month, with a shift
lead, so that they have seen a cold room, a dock and a gate before they speak to
customers about them.

17.4. The customer service lead meets each new agent at the end of their first
month and again at three months.

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,
which carries red sleeve packets, seal books and protective equipment only.
Anything taken from it at night is written on the cupboard sheet and signed for
properly the next morning.

2.3. The Guwahati cage is looked after by the shift lead named by Riniki Bora.
The Coimbatore cage is looked after by the morning shift lead.

2.4. Stores is not a place to wait, eat or charge a phone. Drivers collecting
seal books or sleeves wait at the counter.

## 16. Month-end reporting

16.1. On the third working day of each month, the customer service lead sends
Finance and the account managers a report of the month's tickets by account:
bookings, late vehicles, complaints, credit notes raised and notices sent.

16.2. Each account manager reviews the report for their accounts and writes one
line per account on anything unusual. The lines are sent back to the lead within
two working days.

16.3. The report is not sent to customers as it stands. A customer who wants a
monthly service report gets one written for them by the account manager, from
the same figures.

16.4. Figures in the report come from the customer service system. An agent who
knows a figure is wrong corrects the ticket, not the report.

16.5. The BharatVac and Manjara Dairy accounts get a quarterly review meeting in
addition to the month-end report, held by their account managers with Finance
and QA.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written
VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.

## 18. Audit of Stores

18.1. Finance audits the Nagpur store twice a year without notice, counting a
sample of lines chosen on the day.

18.2. QA audits the numbered stock once a year, from the manufacturer's delivery
note to the gate register and back to the stubs.

18.3. Findings are written up by the auditor and answered by Nalini Patil within
ten working days, with an owner and a date for each action.

18.4. A finding that repeats from one audit to the next is escalated to the
Nagpur DC manager and to Finance.

# Gel packs and passive shippers: terms and figures

## Packs

- **blue-cap pack** — conditioned at +5.0 C; the only pack used for pharma.
- **white-cap pack** — conditioned at -20 C; frozen goods only, never in a shipper with blue-cap packs.
- **cycle** — one conditioning and one use. A pack is retired after 40 cycles; the count is kept by punching the tab on the pack.
- A pack found swollen or leaking is retired whatever its count.

# Gel pack and shipper figures, QA room sheet

Pinned beside conditioning cabinet CC-1.

## Packs

- blue-cap pack — conditioned at +5.0 C, pharma only.
- white-cap pack — conditioned at -20 C, frozen goods only; never mixed with blue caps.
- A pack is retired after 60 cycles.

## Why a cycle limit

Every freeze and thaw works the seam of a pack. A pack that leaks inside a
shipper wets the product box and ruins the label, so packs are retired on a
count, not on how they look.

# Gel packs: why blue caps, 18 hours and a cycle limit

## Why packs are conditioned at +5.0 C, not frozen

The 2025 shipper validation first used packs straight from a freezer. Three of the five trial runs dipped to +1.4 C at the carton nearest a frozen pack.
A vaccine that freezes is lost for good; a warm excursion at least has a
stability letter to argue with.

Blue caps and white caps were chosen because the night team works under one tube light and colour is read faster than a label.

- **packs per shipper** — 22 blue-cap packs.

## Notes from the trial

The trial ran in the night team's slot, because that is when pharma shippers are
made up. White packs from the freezer and blue packs from CC-1 sat on separate
trolleys. One tube light over the bench had failed and was not replaced for a
week. The caps were ordered from the same supplier as the pack bodies.

## Why 18 hours

Packs pulled after 12 hours of conditioning ran warm from about hour 30 of the trial.
At 18 hours every run held range for the length of the lane.

## Shippers

- 18 blue-cap packs go in each shipper.
- Shipper conditioning time: 18 hours at +5.0 C.
- A closed shipper holds its range for 72 hours.

## 5. Instruments that travel south

5.1. Coimbatore has no calibration chamber and no bench master logger. Those
live at Nagpur. What Coimbatore does have is one lab-certified hand-held
thermometer, serial HP-C00, kept locked in the DC manager's cabinet.

5.2. Every hand-held thermometer in daily use at Coimbatore is checked against
HP-C00 every 14 days: both tips go into the same stirred jug of crushed ice and
water, and the two readings must agree within 0.5 C. The shift lead writes both
readings on QCL-F-12 and sends a photograph of the sheet to the Nagpur QA desk.

5.3. The shorter interval is deliberate. Coimbatore has no bench to catch a
drifting instrument quickly, and a second jug check costs nothing but ten
minutes.

5.4. HP-C00 itself goes to Metrosure Labs, Pune, by courier every 12 months.
While it is away, the Nagpur QA desk sends a loan instrument ahead of it, so the
site is never without a certified thermometer.

5.5. USB loggers are not checked at Coimbatore at all. Every spare logger for a
Coimbatore red sleeve is checked at the Nagpur bench and arrives in its sleeve
already stickered. A logger that has been out of date on the shelf is sent back
to Nagpur, never re-used on the strength of a local jug check.

5.6. Infrared guns are used at Coimbatore only to find a warm carton quickly.
They are never the reading that decides anything.

## 3. Swab check

3.1. Three swabs: floor front, floor rear, door gasket.

3.2. Each must read 150 or below on the handheld luminometer. One failed swab means the whole washdown is repeated, not just the failed spot.

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

12.1. Cardboard, stretch wrap and broken pallets are separated at the back of
the south block. A scrap dealer from Kovaipudur collects cardboard and wrap
every Tuesday and pays by the kg.

12.2. Broken pallets are stacked by the east wall for the pallet repairer, who
comes on the first working day of each month.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the
scrap pile. It is not used for anything and it is not to be sold until Finance
writes it off.

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

## Making it up

3. Load the packs in the pattern printed inside the shipper lid, then put the product box in the middle with a USB logger taped to its side.
4. Close the lid and fix a tamper label across the lid seam.
5. Write the shipper number (PS-01 to PS-12), the pack batch and the time the lid was closed in the shipper register.

## Half two: passive shippers

Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock beyond a short limit unless a
validated passive shipper is used; the limit and the exception are clause 8.2 of
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md).

Quillfern has been refusing bookings it could have taken, including chilled
pharma on [RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md), which has no shipper cradle
and therefore cannot take pharma critical stock without one. The pilot puts
twelve validated passive shippers at Nagpur from August 2026.

Hire is charged to the customer per shipper per trip at the rate printed on
[the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md). Finance added that line to the
card when this project was approved, so the card and the project were signed in
the same week.

## 9. Insulated boxes in the load

9.1. A validated passive shipper carries pharma stock inside a reefer body or on
a body without a cradle, such as RF-119.

9.2. A closed shipper is validated for 48 hours from the lid-closing time
written in the shipper register. A shipper that will still be on the road at 40
hours is called in to Fleet Control, and QA decides whether it is re-packed or
the consignment is held.

9.3. The shipper's lid is never opened on the road. The tamper label across the
lid seam is photographed at departure and again at delivery.

9.4. Shippers travel upright, strapped to the body wall, and never under other
freight.

9.5. The empty shipper comes back on the return run in the same condition it
went out, with its packs inside and its logger taped in place, so that QA can
download the logger and count the pack cycles.

## 17. Weather and the seasons

17.1. From June to September the monsoon closes ghat sections and floods low
roads on the Nagpur lanes. Fleet Control reads the weather warnings every
morning and every evening and marks any lane under a red warning on the board.

17.2. A vehicle is not dispatched into a red-warning area unless the customer's
stock cannot wait and the Fleet head has agreed in writing. A late delivery is a
customer problem; a vehicle in a flooded underpass is a Quillfern one.

17.3. Fog on the Nashik and Sinnar roads in December and January slows every run.
Planners add time to those runs in the plan rather than asking drivers to make it
up.

17.4. In April and May the midday heat on the Vidarbha roads is hard on drivers
as well as on reefer units. Planners avoid midday departures on long runs in
those months where the customer's window allows, and every cab carries drinking
water.

17.5. After any storm, drivers report fallen trees, washed-out roads and closed
bridges to Fleet Control, which passes them to the other drivers on the same
lane.

17.6. Guwahati's monsoon runs from June to September and Coimbatore's heavy rain
comes from October to December. Fleet Control plans each DC's runs by its own
season, not by the Nagpur calendar.

**PROJ-124** is open. It has two halves that share a sponsor and a budget line
but nothing else: getting physical red sleeve packets back into every DC, and

The red sleeve is the packet clipped to an excursion file or a pharma truck

The trigger was operational, not a policy gap. Stores had been promising vendor
plastic sleeves "next week" since April 2026, and the Nagpur night team recorded

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccine must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A high
excursion is declared when an approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for
45 continuous minutes.

2.2. A low excursion is declared below +2.0 C for 8 continuous
minutes. Staging time on a covered dock counts towards both.

2.3. Room NRL-F4 is the vaccine room at Visakhapatnam. Quarantine bay NRL-Q6 receives any
stock placed on hold.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion is
declared when any approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion is
declared when the approved record is more than +8.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. An insulin low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.3. Milk and paneer must remain from 0.0 C to +4.0 C while in cold rooms and
reefer bodies. A dairy high excursion is declared when milk or paneer is above
+5.0 C for 30 continuous minutes, including staging time after dock release.

2.4. Frozen food must remain at or below -18.0 C. A frozen-food excursion is
declared when the approved record is warmer than -15.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes.

2.5. The Nagpur central hub is also referred to as "NGP hub" in older records.
For this SOP, Nagpur DC and NGP hub mean the same facility unless a customer
contract names a different annex.

2.6. Legacy staging note retained from revision 2.0: milk crates may remain on a
covered dock until +7.0 C for 45 minutes before QA notice is required. This
paragraph has not been relied on since revision 4.0 and is retained only because
customer annex QF-Dairy-11 still quotes it.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

temperature excursion in its cold rooms, docks, cross-dock lanes and reefer

under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. An excursion means a recorded temperature outside the allowed band for
longer than the allowed duration. One hand-held reading does not release stock.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: why M2, and why nobody goes back

## Why M2 and not the canteen lawn

Until 2024 the ammonia muster point was M1, the canteen lawn. In the July 2024 monsoon drill the windsock put the canteen lawn downwind of the compressor house for four of the six drill hours.
M2, by gate 2, sits upwind under the south-west monsoon wind and has a second
way out on to the ring road. M1 is still the fire muster point.

# Ammonia alarm card, canteen notice board

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks, engines off. Do not drive through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door away from the compressor house.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register within 15 minutes and rings the plant operator on extension 251 with the count.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, phones or trucks.

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop the forklift where it is and switch it off. If a reefer is backing in, the driver stops and switches off.
2. Leave through the dock 5 side door, away from the compressor house.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. Give your name to the shift lead at M2.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, a phone or a truck.

# Ammonia alarm card, dock 5

Dock 5 is the frozen dock and the nearest dock to the compressor house, so this
card hangs at the shutter.

## 6. Where the truck is

6.1. Customers ask where their vehicle is more than they ask anything else.

6.2. Customer service gives an ETA only from Fleet Control's board, rounded to
30 minutes, and never calls the driver.

6.3. If the board shows no position, because of a dead zone, the agent says that
the vehicle is in an area without signal and gives the last known position and
time. The agent does not guess.

6.4. A customer who has the driver's number and calls him directly is asked, the
next time customer service speaks to them, to call customer service instead.
Drivers answer only when parked.

6.5. A late vehicle is reported to the customer as late as soon as Fleet Control
says it will miss its window. The reason is given in plain words and without
blame.

## First day driver checklist

Bring licence, Aadhaar copy, bank details, two photos, and any vendor letter if
you are hired-truck staff. At the gate you sign the safety acknowledgement, get
the dispatch note, confirm seal numbers, and check whether the load is pharma,
dairy, frozen, or dry grocery.

Never troubleshoot a telematics device while driving. Park first. If a manager
says "just reach", call Fleet Control and ask them to record the instruction.

## 11. Complaints and escalation

11.1. A complaint is anything a customer says is wrong with our service, even if
they do not use the word.

11.2. The agent records it, acknowledges it the same day, and passes it to the
account manager. The account manager replies within three working days.

11.3. A complaint about a driver's behaviour goes to Fleet Control and HR, not
to the driver.

11.4. A complaint that mentions safety, such as a vehicle driven fast or a
driver who looked unwell, goes to Fleet Control within the hour, whatever else
the complaint is about.

11.5. A customer who asks for a senior person is given the account manager's
name. If the account manager is away, the customer service lead takes the call.

## Who do I call for a temperature alarm?

In daytime, call QA desk extension 440. At night in Nagpur, call Bunty or the
shift lead on extension 228, then Fleet Control if a truck is moving. For
patient-critical pharma, Compliance-Red is the escalation group after the 2025
drill. Please do not use the old qa-shared mailbox for urgent alarms.

## Which telematics app do we use?

Old training screenshots still show Kalpa. Most old trips are in Kalpa, and the
guard cabin tablet may still be there for audit lookups. For new trips we are
moving to Tessaline; ask IT for the current login because the app names keep
changing.

## Nagpur DC / NGP hub

Book Nagpur slots in Dockwise before 16:00 on the previous day. Pharma uses dock 4, dairy uses docks 1 and 2, and frozen food uses dock 5. The old Kalpa slot sync link on the left is broken and should not be used for new bookings.

No unloading is planned between 13:10 and 13:40 because the ammonia plant runs the daily defrost check. Late arrival goes to holding lane B, call shift lead, no automatic cancellation.

Pharma arrivals get 15 minutes grace. Dairy arrivals get 20 minutes grace. Frozen arrivals get 10 minutes grace because the freezer-to-reefer movement is shorter and more sensitive.

often says "NGP hub".

question: new frozen dock guy at NGP hub — what should he know about the ammonia plant next door

answer_text:
## Why pellets

Quillfern used to buy dry ice in blocks. Blocks had to be broken with a mallet on the dock, and two hand injuries in 2024 came from exactly that.
The blocks came in 12 kg slabs, and staff carried the slabs by hand because no
tote was used for them. The chest lid has two handles. Vidarbha Gases rated
pellets as easier to meter by the kg, and pellets of 16 mm from Vidarbha Gases
replaced blocks in 2024.

## Root cause

The immediate cause was warm air ingress through a torn door curtain and door
opening during dairy cross-dock spillover. The deeper cause was that the Kalpa
alert routing still pointed to the old qa-shared mailbox, which was not watched
by the night team. The shift lead tried to protect the room by placing dry ice
near the curtain, but the team did not quarantine stock until the manager was
awake.

We also found that dock scheduling pushed paneer loading next to the vaccine
cold-room door. This did not create the torn curtain, but it increased door
traffic during the vulnerable period. The dock plan must separate pharma
loading from dairy overflow during night shift.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| item | Coimbatore rule |
|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 02:44 | Bunty placed dry ice trays outside the inner curtain but did not move stock. |

# Dry ice at Quillfern: why the present rules

## Why it stays out of C2 and C3

On the night of 12 March 2025 dry ice trays were set outside the inner curtain
of C2 to hold the room down. The intention was good, but the trays masked the room reading at the curtain and put the vials nearest the door at risk of dropping below +2.0 C.
A pharma room is protected by containment and quarantine, not by cooling it from
the outside.

## 4. Rooms, bays and what lives where

4.1. CBE-PHARMA is the insulin room. It holds insulin only; Coimbatore does not
store vaccines. Room limits and excursion durations are those of the SOP and
are not repeated in this handbook.

4.2. CBE-FROZEN is the freezer. It holds restaurant-chain frozen stock and a
small amount of frozen peas for a Tiruppur wholesaler.

4.3. The chilled dairy room was closed in 2024 when the Coimbatore milk account
moved to a local cooperative. Its door is still in the corridor and is labelled
CLOSED ROOM, NO STOCK. Nothing is put in it, including overflow.

4.4. Quarantine bay Q-C1 is at the north-west corner of the cold block, behind
the red chain. Only QA, through the shift lead on the phone, releases stock from
it.

4.5. Dry grocery is stored in the south block in racks S1 to S6. None of it is
cold chain, and none of it may be stacked against the cold block wall, which
sweats in the monsoon.

4.6. The battery charging bay for FL-C1 and FL-C2 is outside the cold block,
under the annexe stairs. Nobody charges a forklift inside a cold room.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 8. North-east monsoon and the afternoon sun

8.1. Coimbatore's heavy rain comes with the north-east monsoon, from October to
December, not in the June to September months that set the calendar at Nagpur
and Guwahati.

8.2. Rain cover over rear pallets is used at Coimbatore from October to December
whenever it is raining on the apron. The site owns six tarpaulins for this.

8.3. Coimbatore does not bill the customer for rain cover. The monsoon handling
line on the rate card is a Guwahati charge and is not quoted for Coimbatore
loads. Customer service agents who copy the Guwahati line onto a Coimbatore
quotation create a credit note later.

8.4. The hot months are March to May. In those months the afternoon rule in
section 3.5 is enforced strictly, and the wash pad is used before 11:00 so that
washed bodies are not left drying in the midday sun with their doors open.

8.5. The cold block wall sweats in the monsoon. Anything stored against it on
the dry side is moved 30 cm away from the wall from October onwards.

answer_text:
## 7. When the doors are opened on the road

7.1. Police, excise, sales tax and transport officers may stop a loaded reefer
and ask to see the load. Drivers cooperate, and do not argue about cold chain
at the roadside.

7.2. The driver asks for the officer's name and badge number and writes both on
the back of the dispatch note, with the time and place. The driver photographs
the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 20. Transfers between sites

20.1. Stock sent from Nagpur to Guwahati or Coimbatore travels with a Stores
transfer note on QCL-F-45, listing every item and quantity. The receiving cage
counts the parcel on arrival and signs the note.

20.2. A short or damaged transfer is written on the note and photographed before
the parcel is signed for. The courier is told the same day.

20.3. Numbered stock and made-up red sleeve packets travel in sealed courier
bags. The bag number is written on the transfer note.

20.4. Items are never transferred between sites in a driver's cab, even when a
vehicle happens to be going that way, unless the item is on the dispatch note.

20.5. The signed transfer notes come back to Nagpur by scan the same day and by
post at the month end.

## 4. Seal books

4.1. Seals come from the seal manufacturer in books, already numbered in order.
Stores records the first and last number of each book received.

4.2. Stores issues seal books to a DC gate one book at a time against the gate's
signature. Besides the book open at the gate, a gate may hold at most two
unopened books in its locked drawer; a third is not issued until one of the two
is opened.

4.3. Spoiled seals marked VOID come back to Stores with their stubs. Stores
counts the stubs against QCL-F-35 every Friday, and a number that is neither
fitted, spoiled nor on the shelf is reported to Fleet Control the same day.

4.4. Each DC holds two bolt-seal cutters, and a lost cutter is replaced by Stores
within one working day.

4.5. Tamper labels for pharma pallets and shipper lids are issued in rolls of
200 to QA, not to the gate.

4.6. Seal books for Guwahati and Coimbatore go by courier, two books at a time,
and are signed for at the gate cabin on arrival.

## 14. Training and coaching for drivers

14.1. Every new owned-reefer driver rides two supervised runs with an experienced
driver before driving alone. One of the two is a night run.

14.2. The supervised runs cover the cab card, the takeover walk-round, the seal
routine, the red sleeve, the gate checklist for pharma runs and the way to speak
to Fleet Control on the phone. The experienced driver signs the new driver's
training sheet at the end of each run.

14.3. Telematics coaching calls are held within two working days of an alert, as
the policy says. The coach asks what happened before saying anything about what
should have happened.

14.4. Drivers who complete a year with no safety non-conformance receive a
certificate from the Fleet head, presented at the Nagpur driver meeting. The
certificate carries no money and is not tied to arrival times.

14.5. The Nagpur driver meeting is held on the last Saturday of each month in
the driver rest room. Attendance is paid duty time. Drivers on the road that day
receive the notes on their phone.

## 3. Receiving goods

3.1. Goods are received against the purchase order and the delivery note, and
counted before the delivery note is signed. A short delivery is written as short
on the delivery note in front of the supplier's driver.

3.2. Temperature-sensitive consumables, such as conditioned gel packs, are not
received by Stores. They go directly to the QA room.

3.3. Calibrated instruments are received by Stores and passed unopened to the QA
bench on the same day. Stores does not open an instrument box to check it.

3.4. Damaged goods are photographed, set aside and reported to Finance before the
supplier's driver leaves, where that is possible.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written
VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

## 1. What this manual covers

1.1. The manual covers owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans and escort
cars moving under a Quillfern dispatch note, from the moment a vehicle is taken
over at a DC until it is handed back with its paperwork.

1.2. It does not cover warehouse work inside the cold rooms, customer contracts,
or pricing. A driver who is asked a price by a customer refers the customer to
customer service.

1.3. Revision 3 of July 2026 added section 9 on passive shippers in transit and
moved the police-check rules into section 7.

1.4. Where the manual and the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy seem to
differ, the policy applies. Where the manual and the SOP seem to differ on
anything about temperature, the SOP applies.

1.5. Copies of the manual are kept at the Fleet Control desk in Nagpur, in the
gate cabin at each DC and in the driver rest room at Nagpur. Drivers are not
expected to carry it; the cab card carries what a driver needs on the road.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

## 3. Opening an account

3.1. A new customer is opened by an account manager, never by an agent. The
account manager checks the customer's product classes against what each DC can
store and move.

3.2. A customer who needs vaccines stored at Coimbatore is told plainly that
Coimbatore does not store vaccines. A customer who needs chilled dairy stored at
Coimbatore is told the same.

3.3. A customer who wants its own pricing gets a signed annex. Until the annex
is signed, the standard rate card is the only price that may be given.

3.4. The account manager sends the customer the list of named contacts on both
sides, including who will receive an excursion notice at night.

3.5. A customer who asks to be told of every alarm, not only confirmed
excursions, is told that Quillfern notifies confirmed excursions. A customer
wanting alarm-level alerts is referred to the account manager, who may arrange a
Tessaline customer view under the annex.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

## 9. Credit notes

9.1. A credit note is raised by Finance on the account manager's request. Agents
do not promise one.

9.2. A credit note for a wrongly quoted line, such as a Guwahati monsoon line on a
Coimbatore load, is raised without a claim, but still needs the account
manager's request.

9.3. A credit note is never offered to settle a complaint about an excursion
before QA has recorded a disposition.

9.4. Every credit note carries the invoice number, the line and the reason, in
words a customer's accounts clerk can follow without calling us.

# Customer Service Handbook

For customer service agents and account managers at Pune HQ and at the three
DCs. It says how customer service works with customers and with the rest of
Quillfern. It sets no temperature limit, no notification window and no price;
those are in the SOP, the customer notification matrix and the rate card, and an
agent opens those documents rather than quoting this handbook.

## 12. Customer loggers

12.1. Some customers send their own logger with the stock. The logger travels
with the stock from the moment it arrives until it leaves.

12.2. A customer logger does not overrule the Tessaline record. If the customer
quotes their logger in an argument, the agent says that QA will compare the two
files and explain any difference.

12.3. A customer logger sent back to the customer goes with the return challan,
never by separate post.

12.4. The agent never downloads or opens a customer logger. That is QA's work.

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

## Where alerts go

- Cold-room high and low alarms email the qa-shared mailbox at
  qa-shared@quillfern.example. This is the correct destination for every room
  alarm, including vaccine rooms.
- Truck alarms raise an SMS to the Fleet Control rota phone and an email to the
  same qa-shared mailbox.
- There is no separate pharma escalation group. If a vaccine room alarms at
  night, the night lead phones the DC manager and the DC manager decides whether
  to wake QA.

## Findings

1. One shift lead emailed the old qa-shared mailbox before calling Compliance-Red. The obsolete habit is named here, as clause 10.4 of the SOP requires: **qa-shared is not an escalation route.**
2. The red sleeve on RF-118 had no spare logger.
3. The night controller paused his run through [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md) when the alarm sounded; no vehicle left during the drill.
4. Two staff asked what "warm pallet" means. It is defined in [the jargon sheet](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

## Root cause

The immediate cause was warm air ingress through a torn door curtain and door
opening during dairy cross-dock spillover. The deeper cause was that the Kalpa
alert routing still pointed to the old qa-shared mailbox, which was not watched
by the night team. The shift lead tried to protect the room by placing dry ice
near the curtain, but the team did not quarantine stock until the manager was
awake.

We also found that dock scheduling pushed paneer loading next to the vaccine
cold-room door. This did not create the torn curtain, but it increased door
traffic during the vulnerable period. The dock plan must separate pharma
loading from dairy overflow during night shift.

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 02:31 | Alert email went to qa-shared@quillfern.example; no SMS reached Compliance. |

## Known gaps

- Door-open events are unreliable where network coverage is poor. Keep the paper
  driver call log.
- The qa-shared mailbox is not watched overnight. This has been raised twice and
  is listed as accepted risk for 2021.

## Actions

| action | owner | due |
|---|---|---|
| Remove qa-shared from the night desk speed-dial | IT Service Desk | 28 February 2026 |

## Summary

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of
rotavirus vaccine in lots ROTA-9A and ROTA-9B. The approved record showed the
room above +8.0 C for 66 minutes. At the time of the event, the SOP required a
QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

| action | owner | due | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change pharma critical alerts from qa-shared to Compliance-Red SMS and phone tree | IT Service Desk | 18 Mar 2025 | open at time of note |

## Closing note

This event is the reason I am asking for two changes: faster pharma escalation
and a shorter vaccine high-duration trigger. If the telematics vendor changes,
the first acceptance test must prove night alerts reach Compliance-Red, not only
the DC manager.

I have deliberately left the rough timeline language in place because the audit
packet should show how the team understood the event on the day. Later SOP
revisions may be cleaner, but this note is the incident record, not a training
poster. Any future reader should compare it with the live SOP before using its
thresholds.

# Dry ice: properties and limits

## What it is

- **dry ice** — solid carbon dioxide. At normal pressure it turns straight into gas at -78.5 C; it does not melt into a liquid.
- **pellet** — the 16 mm form Quillfern buys from Vidarbha Gases.
- **sublimation loss** — stock that turns to gas while waiting; about 8% of the chest's contents a day with the lid shut.

## Loss in the chest

A frozen chest is not the same as a dry-ice chest: the dry-ice chest is
insulated but not refrigerated. Loss is higher on a body top-up day, when the
lid is opened more often. A kg lost to the air is still written on QCL-F-26 at
the weekly count, so the store knows what the body jobs really cost.

# Dry ice handling card, dock 5 board

Printed for the board beside dock 5, where frozen top-ups are loaded.

## Before you touch it

Cryogenic gloves and face shield from the rack beside the chest. No cotton
gloves, no bare hands.

## Taking it out

1. Sign the pellets out on QCL-F-26 with the kg, the job and your name.
2. Scoop the pellets into an insulated tote. Never put dry ice in a sealed box, a flask or a drum with a screw lid.
3. A load above 10 kg is carried by two people.
4. Dry ice never travels in a driver's cab, and never goes into cold room C2 or C3.

## If the monitor beeps

If the CO2 monitor over the chest beeps, leave the room, shut the door and call the shift lead.

# Dry ice handling at Nagpur stores and docks

## Before you touch it

Wear cryogenic gloves and the face shield from the rack beside the chest; cotton gloves and bare hands are never acceptable.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

## 4. Seal books

4.1. Seals come from the seal manufacturer in books, already numbered in order.
Stores records the first and last number of each book received.

4.2. Stores issues seal books to a DC gate one book at a time against the gate's
signature. Besides the book open at the gate, a gate may hold at most two
unopened books in its locked drawer; a third is not issued until one of the two
is opened.

4.3. Spoiled seals marked VOID come back to Stores with their stubs. Stores
counts the stubs against QCL-F-35 every Friday, and a number that is neither
fitted, spoiled nor on the shelf is reported to Fleet Control the same day.

4.4. Each DC holds two bolt-seal cutters, and a lost cutter is replaced by Stores
within one working day.

4.5. Tamper labels for pharma pallets and shipper lids are issued in rolls of
200 to QA, not to the gate.

4.6. Seal books for Guwahati and Coimbatore go by courier, two books at a time,
and are signed for at the gate cabin on arrival.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 7. When the doors are opened on the road

7.1. Police, excise, sales tax and transport officers may stop a loaded reefer
and ask to see the load. Drivers cooperate, and do not argue about cold chain
at the roadside.

7.2. The driver asks for the officer's name and badge number and writes both on
the back of the dispatch note, with the time and place. The driver photographs
the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 13. Language and new people

13.1. Coimbatore works in Tamil. Training is given by a trainer in Tamil, with
English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not
put on the late shift, and never left alone in the cold block, until a shift
lead has signed them off.

13.3. Every new joiner is shown the gate cabin, the security roster and the key
register on the first day. They are told that security will not open anything
for them at night except in an emergency, and that the lockers, the cabinet and
the seal drawer are all separate keys.

13.4. New drivers from hired-truck vendors are shown the south gate routine by
the guard and the Temple Street timing by the shift lead before their first
booking.

13.5. The words used on site follow the company glossary. A new joiner who hears
a word they do not know is expected to ask, on any shift, and nobody at
Coimbatore is to laugh at the question.

## 4. Taking over a vehicle

4.1. The driver taking over a vehicle walks round it with the driver handing
over, or with the shift lead if the vehicle was parked empty.

4.2. The walk-round covers tyres and wheel nuts, lights, mirrors, the reefer
unit's display and alarm light, the rear door hasp, the cab locker and the red
sleeve, the fire extinguisher, and the wheel chocks.

4.3. Any damage found on the walk-round is photographed and written on the
takeover sheet before the vehicle moves. Damage found later is presumed to have
happened on the later driver's watch.

4.4. The cab card is checked for the current Fleet Control, QA desk and
Compliance-Red numbers. A cab card printed before the Tessaline cutover is
replaced before the vehicle leaves.

4.5. The driver checks that the Tessaline unit shows the vehicle's own asset
number. Units have been swapped between vehicles in the workshop and not
re-labelled.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written
VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

## 17. Handover between storekeepers

17.1. A storekeeper going on leave for more than two days hands over to the
other storekeeper with a walk round the cage and a signed note of open requests,
expected deliveries and any count differences not yet closed.

17.2. The keys to the cage are signed over in the key book at the handover, with
the time.

17.3. Nalini Patil's own leave is covered by the Nagpur DC manager's nominee, who
signs the key book and the handover note like anyone else.

## 8. Dry ice supply

8.1. Stores places the standing order for dry ice at Nagpur. Vidarbha Gases
delivers 120 kg on Monday and Thursday mornings, and extra deliveries are
ordered by Stores on the shift lead's request.

8.2. Stores does not hold dry ice in the store. The delivery goes straight to
the dry-ice chest, where the shift lead signs the delivery note.

8.3. At the weekly count Stores records the kg delivered, the kg signed out on
QCL-F-26 and the kg left in the chest, and the difference is recorded as
sublimation loss.

8.4. Guwahati and Coimbatore order their own dry ice from their local suppliers,
and send Stores the delivery notes monthly.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

# Dry ice handling at Nagpur stores and docks

## Before you touch it

Wear cryogenic gloves and the face shield from the rack beside the chest; cotton gloves and bare hands are never acceptable.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 9. Protective equipment

9.1. Stores issues cryogenic gloves, face shields, freezer suits, safety shoes,
high-visibility vests and hearing protection against a signature.

9.2. Freezer suits are issued to named people, not to a shift. A suit that no
longer closes properly is returned and replaced.

9.3. Cryogenic gloves and face shields for dry-ice work are not personal issue.
They hang on the rack beside each chest and are replaced by Stores when damaged.

9.4. Safety shoes are replaced once a year, or sooner if the sole is split.

9.5. Hired-truck drivers are issued a high-visibility vest at the gate and return
it at the gate.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

5.5. Packets ordered under the red sleeve project are recorded against that

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

pharma critical event at any hour, the shift lead calls Compliance-Red as at
every other site.

2.5. Fleet Control is in Nagpur on extension 301. Coimbatore has no fleet desk
of its own; the shift lead is Fleet Control's eyes on the apron.

2.6. The site landline goes to the office annexe. After 22:00 it diverts to the
gate cabin, and the guard answers it with the site name only, never with a
person's name.

## Why a second pair of hands

The tote handles are rated for 12 kg, so one person with a full tote is already at the limit of the handles.
A dropped tote on a wet dock scatters pellets that people then pick up with the
wrong gloves.

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

12.1. Cardboard, stretch wrap and broken pallets are separated at the back of
the south block. A scrap dealer from Kovaipudur collects cardboard and wrap
every Tuesday and pays by the kg.

12.2. Broken pallets are stacked by the east wall for the pallet repairer, who
comes on the first working day of each month.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the
scrap pile. It is not used for anything and it is not to be sold until Finance
writes it off.

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

# Dry ice handling at Nagpur stores and docks

## Before you touch it

Wear cryogenic gloves and the face shield from the rack beside the chest; cotton gloves and bare hands are never acceptable.

# Dry ice at Quillfern: why the present rules

## Why it stays out of C2 and C3

On the night of 12 March 2025 dry ice trays were set outside the inner curtain
of C2 to hold the room down. The intention was good, but the trays masked the room reading at the curtain and put the vials nearest the door at risk of dropping below +2.0 C.
A pharma room is protected by containment and quarantine, not by cooling it from
the outside.

# Probe calibration: why the ice-point bench

## What we had

Until July 2025 every hand-held probe went to Metrosure Labs, Pune, once a
quarter. Each lab round took the probes away for 9 working days, at Rs. 1,450 per probe per visit.
With 64 probes across three DCs that came to Rs. 3.71 lakh a year, and the
probes were away exactly when the night shifts needed them.

## What was chosen

A monthly ice-point check at the Nagpur QA bench, with one external lab
calibration a year kept for traceability. The BharatVac annex QF-Pharma-04 asks
for a traceable certificate on every instrument used as evidence, and quotes
±0.5 C for hand-held instruments; the bench pass band was set to match. USB
loggers are held tighter, at 0.3 C, because in a dispute the logger file is the
evidence and the probe is only the first look.

# Probe calibration: terms and tolerances

## Terms

- **ice point** — 0.0 C, the temperature of a stirred slurry of crushed ice and potable water.
- **bench master** — the lab-certified logger kept in the QA calibration chamber at Nagpur, serial UL-M01, recertified every 12 months by Metrosure Labs.
- **drift** — the change in an instrument's error between two checks.
- **pass band** — the largest error an instrument may show and still be used.

## 7. Gel packs and shipper consumables

7.1. Stores buys gel packs and holds them unconditioned. Conditioning happens in
the QA room, not in Stores.

7.2. Stores keeps at least 44 unconditioned blue-cap packs at Nagpur, enough to
remake two shippers completely.

7.3. Packs retired by QA, for cycle count or for damage, are sent to the
supplier for disposal and recorded as written off. Stores does not throw them in
general waste, because the gel is not general waste.

7.4. White-cap packs are held on a separate shelf, labelled FROZEN GOODS ONLY.

7.5. Spare shipper lids, straps and liners are held by Stores and issued to QA
against a signature. A damaged shipper body is not repaired in Stores.

## 14. Layout and labelling of the store

14.1. The Nagpur store is laid out in four zones: numbered stock in the locked
cage, instruments on the shelf beside the QA hatch, protective equipment on the
open racks, and general consumables at the back.

14.2. Every shelf carries a printed label with the item name, the Stores item
code and the minimum stock. A handwritten label is replaced within a week.

14.3. Heavy items are stored below waist height. Nothing is stored on top of the
cage or on the floor of the walkway.

14.4. The store floor is swept daily and the racks are dusted monthly. Wet items
are never brought into the store; they are dried outside first.

14.5. The Guwahati and Coimbatore cages follow the same labels and item codes as
Nagpur, so that a count sheet from any site reads the same way.

## Why blue and white caps

Blue caps and white caps were chosen because the night team works under one tube light and colour is read faster than a label.

# Gel packs and passive shippers: terms and figures

## Packs

- **blue-cap pack** — conditioned at +5.0 C; the only pack used for pharma.
- **white-cap pack** — conditioned at -20 C; frozen goods only, never in a shipper with blue-cap packs.
- **cycle** — one conditioning and one use. A pack is retired after 40 cycles; the count is kept by punching the tab on the pack.
- A pack found swollen or leaking is retired whatever its count.

## Shippers

- **shipper conditioning time** — 18 hours at +5.0 C, for every pack in the shipper.
- **packs per shipper** — 22 blue-cap packs.
- **shipper fleet** — PS-01 to PS-12, at Nagpur.

## What RF-120 may carry

RF-120 carries frozen food only: frozen restaurant-chain loads, frozen peas and
frozen chicken on the Nagpur intercity lanes.

**RF-120 must never be loaded with vaccines, insulin, milk or paneer.** A frozen
body cannot be run warm for a chilled load, and a chilled load in a frozen body
is a product loss whether or not a sensor alarms. If a chilled consignment is
offered to RF-120 at the gate, the dock team refuses the load and calls Fleet
Control; the dock team may not reclassify the stock to make the booking work.

The frozen target, the excursion threshold and the defrost allowance that apply
to RF-120 are in the `owned_reefer_frozen` truck profile of
[the legacy sensor threshold file](02-sensor-thresholds.yaml), and the excursion
definition that governs a dispute is clause 2.4 of
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). This
file deliberately repeats neither, because the two have disagreed before.

## What RF-118 may carry

RF-118 is a chilled asset. It may carry vaccines, insulin, milk and paneer. It
must not be loaded with frozen food: the body cannot hold the frozen target and
the frozen profile belongs to [RF-120](18-reefer-RF-120-asset-file.md).

This file sets no temperature limit of its own. Every limit and every excursion
duration for the products RF-118 carries is in
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md), and
the sensor configuration is documented in
[the legacy sensor threshold file](02-sensor-thresholds.yaml). Where this file
and the SOP appear to differ, the SOP wins.

# Reefer asset file RF-120

Asset **RF-120** is the owned frozen reefer at Nagpur DC. It is the newest of the
three RF-11x assets and the only one on the frozen profile;
[RF-118](16-reefer-RF-118-asset-file.md) and
[RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md) are chilled bodies and cannot hold the
frozen target. RF-120 was commissioned on 2 December 2025 and went into service
directly on Tessaline, so it has no Kalpa trip history at all.

## Dock and staging

RF-120 loads at dock 5 at Nagpur, per
[Dock scheduling rules 2026](13-dock-scheduling-rules-2026.md). Frozen stock
moves directly between freezer and reefer body; the short delay allowance before
the shift lead must be called is in
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md), clause 8.4.

Frozen arrivals get the shortest grace of any class at Nagpur, which is why a
late RF-120 is called in rather than left in the queue.

## 5. Diesel, cards and the reefer tank

5.1. Every owned reefer carries one fuel card for the truck and one for the

5.2. Drivers fill only at Quillfern-listed pumps. The list is printed on the

otherwise the driver's judgement, with the rule that no vehicle is allowed to
run so low that it must stop somewhere unlit.

5.5. Fuel slips are photographed at the pump and the photograph is sent to
Fleet Control while parked. The paper slip goes into the trip bag.

5.6. A card that is refused at a listed pump is reported to Fleet Control, and
the driver waits for Fleet Control to authorise a payment. Drivers do not pay
for diesel from their own money.

5. A test alarm is sent to Compliance-Red from the vehicle's Tessaline unit, and the QA night phone confirms receipt before the seal goes on.

7. Diesel is at least three-quarters of a tank, and the reefer unit's own fuel tank is full.

8. The seal is photographed with the dock clock in frame.
