## 6. Roadside trouble

6.1. A driver whose vehicle develops a fault stops at a safe place first and
calls second. A lit fuel plaza, a toll rest area or a police post is a safe
place; a road shoulder at night is not, unless the vehicle cannot be moved.

6.2. Roadside tyre changes on a loaded reefer are done by the listed tyre
vendor, never by the driver alone, and Fleet Control expects the vendor within
3 hours on a qualified lane.

6.3. A reefer unit fault is reported with the display reading, the alarm code
and the time. Fleet Control decides whether to send the mobile service van,
transfer the load, or bring the vehicle in. The driver does not open the reefer
unit's panel.

6.4. A breakdown on a lane where the fuel pumps are a quarter of a day apart
makes the wait long. Drivers on such lanes carry water and a torch, and the
mobile service van is not always the quickest help; sometimes the relief point
vendor on the lane arrives first.

6.5. A vehicle that cannot be moved and is carrying pharma critical stock is
reported to Compliance-Red by Fleet Control within the SOP's notification
window, whatever the cause.

6.6. After any roadside repair, the vehicle is walked round again before it
moves, as if it were being taken over.

## 17. Weather and the seasons

17.1. From June to September the monsoon closes ghat sections and floods low
roads on the Nagpur lanes. Fleet Control reads the weather warnings every
morning and every evening and marks any lane under a red warning on the board.

17.2. A vehicle is not dispatched into a red-warning area unless the customer's
stock cannot wait and the Fleet head has agreed in writing. A late delivery is a
customer problem; a vehicle in a flooded underpass is a Quillfern one.

17.3. Fog on the Nashik and Sinnar roads in December and January slows every run.
Planners add time to those runs in the plan rather than asking drivers to make it
up.

17.4. In April and May the midday heat on the Vidarbha roads is hard on drivers
as well as on reefer units. Planners avoid midday departures on long runs in
those months where the customer's window allows, and every cab carries drinking
water.

17.5. After any storm, drivers report fallen trees, washed-out roads and closed
bridges to Fleet Control, which passes them to the other drivers on the same
lane.

17.6. Guwahati's monsoon runs from June to September and Coimbatore's heavy rain
comes from October to December. Fleet Control plans each DC's runs by its own
season, not by the Nagpur calendar.

## 13. Cabs, bodies and how they look

13.1. A Quillfern cab is kept clean enough that a customer's receiving clerk can
sit in it to sign papers. Food wrappers, bottles and bedding are cleared out at
the end of every duty day.

13.2. Nothing is stuck to the windscreen except the permits the law requires and
the Quillfern asset number. Stickers, pictures and hanging charms that block the
driver's view are removed at the takeover walk-round.

13.3. The outside of the body is washed at least once a week, and after any run
through a construction zone or mud. A body whose company markings cannot be read
is washed before its next customer drop.

13.4. Scratches and dents are reported, not painted over. Fleet Control books
body repairs in batches so that no vehicle is off the road longer than it needs
to be.

13.5. The cab card, the red sleeve and the fire extinguisher each have a fixed
place in the cab. A driver who finds any of them moved puts it back and tells
Fleet Control, because the next driver will look for it in its fixed place in a
hurry.

## 14. Training and coaching for drivers

14.1. Every new owned-reefer driver rides two supervised runs with an experienced
driver before driving alone. One of the two is a night run.

14.2. The supervised runs cover the cab card, the takeover walk-round, the seal
routine, the red sleeve, the gate checklist for pharma runs and the way to speak
to Fleet Control on the phone. The experienced driver signs the new driver's
training sheet at the end of each run.

14.3. Telematics coaching calls are held within two working days of an alert, as
the policy says. The coach asks what happened before saying anything about what
should have happened.

14.4. Drivers who complete a year with no safety non-conformance receive a
certificate from the Fleet head, presented at the Nagpur driver meeting. The
certificate carries no money and is not tied to arrival times.

14.5. The Nagpur driver meeting is held on the last Saturday of each month in
the driver rest room. Attendance is paid duty time. Drivers on the road that day
receive the notes on their phone.

## Why number order

Taking seals strictly in number order is what lets an auditor see a gap. A seal
taken from the middle of a book hides a missing one.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

## 15. Visitors and audits

15.1. Every visitor signs the visitor book at the gate cabin and wears a visitor
badge for the whole visit. A visitor who has not signed in is not shown round,
whoever they say they are.

15.2. Customer auditors are escorted by the DC manager or a shift lead from the
gate to the gate. They may look at any room and any record they ask for, but
they do not handle stock and they do not enter a cold room without a freezer
jacket from the rack by the corridor.

15.3. Photographs inside the cold block are taken only with the DC manager's
permission, and only of the thing being audited. A customer's stock is never
photographed for another customer.

15.4. Auditors from the landlord's insurer visit once a year. They look at the
building, the fire equipment and the roof units, not at the cold chain. The DC
manager keeps the fire extinguisher service tags and the roof unit service
sheets in one folder for them.

15.5. After any audit the DC manager writes a short note of what was asked,
what was shown and what was promised, and sends it to Revathi Iyer and Farhan
Qureshi the same week. Promises made to an auditor are kept in that note, not
in anyone's memory.

15.6. School and college groups are not shown round the cold block. Requests
for such visits are passed to Pune HQ.

## 4. Taking over a vehicle

4.1. The driver taking over a vehicle walks round it with the driver handing
over, or with the shift lead if the vehicle was parked empty.

4.2. The walk-round covers tyres and wheel nuts, lights, mirrors, the reefer
unit's display and alarm light, the rear door hasp, the cab locker and the red
sleeve, the fire extinguisher, and the wheel chocks.

4.3. Any damage found on the walk-round is photographed and written on the
takeover sheet before the vehicle moves. Damage found later is presumed to have
happened on the later driver's watch.

4.4. The cab card is checked for the current Fleet Control, QA desk and
Compliance-Red numbers. A cab card printed before the Tessaline cutover is
replaced before the vehicle leaves.

4.5. The driver checks that the Tessaline unit shows the vehicle's own asset
number. Units have been swapped between vehicles in the workshop and not
re-labelled.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

# Gel packs and passive shippers: terms and figures

## Packs

- **blue-cap pack** — conditioned at +5.0 C; the only pack used for pharma.
- **white-cap pack** — conditioned at -20 C; frozen goods only, never in a shipper with blue-cap packs.
- **cycle** — one conditioning and one use. A pack is retired after 40 cycles; the count is kept by punching the tab on the pack.
- A pack found swollen or leaking is retired whatever its count.

# Gel pack and shipper figures, QA room sheet

Pinned beside conditioning cabinet CC-1.

## Packs

- blue-cap pack — conditioned at +5.0 C, pharma only.
- white-cap pack — conditioned at -20 C, frozen goods only; never mixed with blue caps.
- A pack is retired after 60 cycles.

## Why blue and white caps

Blue caps and white caps were chosen because the night team works under one tube light and colour is read faster than a label.

## Notes from the trial

The trial ran in the night team's slot, because that is when pharma shippers are
made up. White packs from the freezer and blue packs from CC-1 sat on separate
trolleys. One tube light over the bench had failed and was not replaced for a
week. The caps were ordered from the same supplier as the pack bodies.

# Gel packs: why blue caps, 18 hours and a cycle limit

## Why packs are conditioned at +5.0 C, not frozen

The 2025 shipper validation first used packs straight from a freezer. Three of the five trial runs dipped to +1.4 C at the carton nearest a frozen pack.
A vaccine that freezes is lost for good; a warm excursion at least has a
stability letter to argue with.

## Shippers

- **shipper conditioning time** — 18 hours at +5.0 C, for every pack in the shipper.
- **packs per shipper** — 22 blue-cap packs.
- **shipper fleet** — PS-01 to PS-12, at Nagpur.

## Shippers

- 18 blue-cap packs go in each shipper.
- Shipper conditioning time: 18 hours at +5.0 C.
- A closed shipper holds its range for 72 hours.

## Why a cycle limit

Every freeze and thaw works the seam of a pack. A pack that leaks inside a
shipper wets the product box and ruins the label, so packs are retired on a
count, not on how they look.

## Why 18 hours

Packs pulled after 12 hours of conditioning ran warm from about hour 30 of the trial.
At 18 hours every run held range for the length of the lane.

## 8. North-east monsoon and the afternoon sun

8.1. Coimbatore's heavy rain comes with the north-east monsoon, from October to
December, not in the June to September months that set the calendar at Nagpur
and Guwahati.

8.2. Rain cover over rear pallets is used at Coimbatore from October to December
whenever it is raining on the apron. The site owns six tarpaulins for this.

8.3. Coimbatore does not bill the customer for rain cover. The monsoon handling
line on the rate card is a Guwahati charge and is not quoted for Coimbatore
loads. Customer service agents who copy the Guwahati line onto a Coimbatore
quotation create a credit note later.

8.4. The hot months are March to May. In those months the afternoon rule in
section 3.5 is enforced strictly, and the wash pad is used before 11:00 so that
washed bodies are not left drying in the midday sun with their doors open.

8.5. The cold block wall sweats in the monsoon. Anything stored against it on
the dry side is moved 30 cm away from the wall from October onwards.

## 3. Guwahati DC

3.1. Guwahati moved from phone slots to Dockwise on 1 February 2026. Riniki Bora
still confirms night slots by phone when the VPN is down, and the slot is written
on the guard register as before.

3.2. Do not idle reefers inside the small yard after 21:30. Rain cover over rear
pallets is mandatory during monsoon unloading and is now billed as a handling
line.

stock cannot wait and the Fleet head has agreed in writing. A late delivery is a

17.5. After any storm, drivers report fallen trees, washed-out roads and closed

17.6. Guwahati's monsoon runs from June to September and Coimbatore's heavy rain

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| item | Coimbatore rule |
|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

## 1. What this manual covers

1.1. The manual covers owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans and escort
cars moving under a Quillfern dispatch note, from the moment a vehicle is taken
over at a DC until it is handed back with its paperwork.

1.2. It does not cover warehouse work inside the cold rooms, customer contracts,
or pricing. A driver who is asked a price by a customer refers the customer to
customer service.

1.3. Revision 3 of July 2026 added section 9 on passive shippers in transit and
moved the police-check rules into section 7.

1.4. Where the manual and the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy seem to
differ, the policy applies. Where the manual and the SOP seem to differ on
anything about temperature, the SOP applies.

1.5. Copies of the manual are kept at the Fleet Control desk in Nagpur, in the
gate cabin at each DC and in the driver rest room at Nagpur. Drivers are not
expected to carry it; the cab card carries what a driver needs on the road.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 4. Coimbatore DC

4.1. Use the south gate for reefers. Avoid Temple Street between 07:45 and 08:30.

4.2. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. Coimbatore joined Dockwise on
1 February 2026 with Guwahati.

## 5. What this document does not do

5.1. It does not set any temperature limit, staging allowance, or excursion
definition. Those live in QCL-QA-SOP-17 and a dock booking never overrules them.

5.2. It does not change driver hours. A slot that cannot be met inside the
driver's remaining hours is rebooked, not driven to.

# Ammonia plant at Nagpur: levels, places and kit

## Alarm levels

- about 5 ppm — the smell is noticeable; not an alarm.
- Stage 1 — 25 ppm at any plant-room detector: amber beacon, the plant crew investigate, and dock 5 stops loading.
- Stage 2 — 150 ppm at any detector: site siren and full evacuation to M2.
- 300 ppm — immediately dangerous to life or health; nobody without a breathing set is anywhere near it.

## 1. Nagpur DC, also written NGP hub

1.1. Book Nagpur slots in Dockwise before 15:00 on the previous day. The old
16:00 cut-off moved because the ammonia plant defrost window moved.

1.2. Dock assignment: pharma uses dock 4, dairy uses docks 1 and 2, frozen food

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

## Books and register

- **seal book** — 25 seals in number order. Only one book is open at the gate at a time.
- **QCL-F-35** — the seal register; one line per seal fitted, cut or spoiled.
- **VOID** — a seal spoiled while fitting; it is cut, bagged with its stub and never reused.
- **trip bag** — the bag that travels back with the dispatch note and holds the cut seals from that trip.

# Seals and tamper labels: types and codes

## Types

- **bolt seal** — a steel bolt and barrel, used once, fitted to the rear door hasp of an owned reefer. Prefix QB, six digits, for example QB-204117.
- **cable seal** — a steel cable locked through the hasp of a hired truck. Prefix QC.
- **tamper label** — an adhesive label that tears if lifted, fixed across the stretch wrap of pharma pallets and the lid seam of passive shippers. Prefix QP.

## Books

- A seal book holds 50 seals in number order.
- Two books may be open at the gate, one for each lane.

## Why number order

Taking seals strictly in number order is what lets an auditor see a gap. A seal
taken from the middle of a book hides a missing one.

| cable seal | QC |

# Seal and label card, stores counter

Hangs at the Stores counter where seal books and label rolls are handed over.

## Fitting at the gate

1. Take the next seal in number order; never skip a number.
2. Bolt seal on owned reefers, cable seal on hired trucks.
3. Record the number on the dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.
4. Photograph the seal with the dock clock in frame.

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,

stay outside and are counted by the guard.

## 15. Visitors and audits

15.1. Every visitor signs the visitor book at the gate cabin and wears a visitor
badge for the whole visit. A visitor who has not signed in is not shown round,
whoever they say they are.

15.2. Customer auditors are escorted by the DC manager or a shift lead from the
gate to the gate. They may look at any room and any record they ask for, but
they do not handle stock and they do not enter a cold room without a freezer
jacket from the rack by the corridor.

15.3. Photographs inside the cold block are taken only with the DC manager's
permission, and only of the thing being audited. A customer's stock is never
photographed for another customer.

15.4. Auditors from the landlord's insurer visit once a year. They look at the
building, the fire equipment and the roof units, not at the cold chain. The DC
manager keeps the fire extinguisher service tags and the roof unit service
sheets in one folder for them.

15.5. After any audit the DC manager writes a short note of what was asked,
what was shown and what was promised, and sends it to Revathi Iyer and Farhan
Qureshi the same week. Promises made to an auditor are kept in that note, not
in anyone's memory.

for such visits are passed to Pune HQ.

7.1. Stores buys gel packs and holds them unconditioned. Conditioning happens in
the QA room, not in Stores.

## Why blue and white caps

Blue caps and white caps were chosen because the night team works under one tube light and colour is read faster than a label.

Every freeze and thaw works the seam of a pack. A pack that leaks inside a
shipper wets the product box and ruins the label, so packs are retired on a
count, not on how they look.

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

# Seals and tamper labels: types and codes

## Types

- **bolt seal** — a steel bolt and barrel, used once, fitted to the rear door hasp of an owned reefer. Prefix QB, six digits, for example QB-204117.
- **cable seal** — a steel cable locked through the hasp of a hired truck. Prefix QC.
- **tamper label** — an adhesive label that tears if lifted, fixed across the stretch wrap of pharma pallets and the lid seam of passive shippers. Prefix QP.

# Seal and label card, stores counter

Hangs at the Stores counter where seal books and label rolls are handed over.

## Fitting at the gate

1. Take the next seal in number order; never skip a number.
2. Bolt seal on owned reefers, cable seal on hired trucks.
3. Record the number on the dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.
4. Photograph the seal with the dock clock in frame.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

A frozen chest is not the same as a dry-ice chest: the dry-ice chest is

- **dry ice** — solid carbon dioxide. At normal pressure it turns straight into gas at -78.5 C; it does not melt into a liquid.

- **sublimation loss** — stock that turns to gas while waiting; about 8% of the chest's contents a day with the lid shut.

## 2. Daily limits

2.1. No driver shall be planned for more than 12 hours on duty in a duty day.
The driving component inside that duty day shall not exceed 9 hours.

2.2. No driver shall drive for more than 4 hours and 30 minutes continuously
without a break of at least 30 minutes. Loading supervision does not count as
the break if the driver is responsible for vehicle movement or seal watching.

2.3. Night driving between 22:00 and 05:00 shall not exceed 6 hours for a
single-driver vehicle. A two-driver vehicle may cover the night segment only if
both drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure.

2.4. A minimum rest period of 11 consecutive hours is required between duty
days. Sleeping in the driver's seat while waiting for a dock is not counted as
the 11-hour rest unless Fleet Control has released the driver and the vehicle is
parked in a safe rest location.

2.5. Every driver must receive one 24-hour weekly rest period in each rolling
seven-day period. Fleet Control shall plan the rest, not discover the breach
after payroll.

2.6. Festival shuttle amendment (amended by Meera Krishnan on 10 June 2026):
for approved religious festival shuttle rosters only, rest may be split into
7 hours plus 4 hours inside the same 24-hour period, provided Fleet Control
approves before dispatch and the driver signs consent after being offered normal
rest.

## 1. Daily limits

1.1. No driver shall be planned for more than 10 hours on duty in a duty day.
The driving component shall not exceed 8 hours.

1.2. No driver shall drive more than 5 hours continuously without a break of at
least 20 minutes.

1.3. A minimum rest period of 9 consecutive hours is required between duty days.

1.4. Weekly rest is one full day in each calendar week. Fleet Control plans it
with the depot roster.

## Standing instructions

- **Night pharma runs.** Fleet Control's standing instruction for RF-118 is a
  two-driver dispatch for any pharma critical night segment, because a single
  driver cannot legally cover the whole Nagpur-Pune night leg. The limit itself
  is in [the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md),
  clause 2.3, and this file does not restate it.
- **Red sleeve.** The red sleeve lives in the cab locker, never in the load
  compartment. Contents are listed in
  [the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md), clause 4.2.
- **Docks.** RF-118 books dock 4 at Nagpur for pharma and docks 1 or 2 for
  dairy, per [Dock scheduling rules 2026](13-dock-scheduling-rules-2026.md).

## 3. Exceptions

3.1. Where weather or police action would cause a driver to exceed a limit, the
driver reports to Fleet Control by phone and Fleet Control decides. There is no
exception code and no written exception form in this policy.

3.2. A cold-chain emergency is a valid reason to extend driving hours with Fleet
head approval. This clause was removed in later policy and must not be applied.

## 4. Conduct

4.1. Mobile phone use while driving is discouraged.

4.2. Seat belts are mandatory for the driver.

4.3. Alcohol is prohibited during duty and for four hours before duty.

# Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy

This policy is in force from 1 May 2026 for all Quillfern employees, contracted
drivers, and hired-truck drivers operating under a Quillfern dispatch note. The
frontmatter says draft because HR has not migrated the policy library; it is not
a licence to ignore the clauses below.

# Driver Hours and Road Discipline Policy (2019)

Issued to all Quillfern drivers and hired-truck providers. Kept for record.

## 8. Records

8.1. Dispatch notes, Tessaline or Kalpa trip reports, driver call logs, exception
forms, and gate registers together form the driving-hours record.

8.2. Records must be kept for three years. Where a pharma critical excursion,
crash, insurance claim, or police matter is involved, the record must be kept
for seven years.

8.3. Fleet and HR jointly review this policy every April. Emergency amendments
may be issued by the Fleet head, but HR must publish them within five working
days.

## 1. Scope

1.1. The policy applies to owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans, escort
cars used for pharma critical movement, and any vehicle carrying Quillfern staff
between a DC, customer site, toll plaza, hotel, or repair yard.

1.2. A driver is on duty from the first required report at gate, yard, hotel, or
customer premises until the vehicle is parked, keys are handed over or secured,
documents are deposited, and the driver is released by Fleet Control.

1.3. A customer request, delayed dock slot, vaccine urgency, milk spoilage risk,
or senior manager's impatience does not cancel this policy. NO LOAD IS WORTH A
LIFE.

## Known history

On the night of 9 February 2026 the Tessaline display on RF-118 jumped between
9.8 C and 3.4 C inside one minute while a hand-held gun read 3.4 C and a spare
logger read 3.6 C on the same insulin carton. The night team kept the original
sensor in place and put the spare logger next to the product, which is what
section 9 of [the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md) requires, and refused
the driver's request to restart the app. The sensor was re-seated on 11 February
2026 under maintenance ticket NGP-MNT-731 and the alarm history was not closed
until QA had the export.

RF-118 also appears in the Nagpur night handover log for 18 October 2025, when
its driver asked what Compliance-Red means. Fleet Control has since printed the
escalation groups on the RF-118 cab card.

8.2. Stores does not hold dry ice in the store. The delivery goes straight to
the dry-ice chest, where the shift lead signs the delivery note.

8.3. At the weekly count Stores records the kg delivered, the kg signed out on
QCL-F-26 and the kg left in the chest, and the difference is recorded as
sublimation loss.

8.4. Guwahati and Coimbatore order their own dry ice from their local suppliers,
and send Stores the delivery notes monthly.

# Dry ice: properties and limits

## What it is

- **dry ice** — solid carbon dioxide. At normal pressure it turns straight into gas at -78.5 C; it does not melt into a liquid.
- **pellet** — the 16 mm form Quillfern buys from Vidarbha Gases.
- **sublimation loss** — stock that turns to gas while waiting; about 8% of the chest's contents a day with the lid shut.

## Limits

| item | limit |
|---|---|
| frozen body top-up | at most 40 kg per body per trip |

## Loss in the chest

A frozen chest is not the same as a dry-ice chest: the dry-ice chest is
insulated but not refrigerated. Loss is higher on a body top-up day, when the
lid is opened more often. A kg lost to the air is still written on QCL-F-26 at
the weekly count, so the store knows what the body jobs really cost.

## 15. Purchase requests and approval limits

15.1. A shift lead or QA officer who needs an item Stores does not hold raises a
purchase request on QCL-F-44 with the item, the quantity, the reason and the date
it is needed.

15.2. Stores checks whether the item is already on an approved purchase order.
If it is, Stores orders against that order. If it is not, the request goes to
Finance.

15.3. Requests up to Rs. 25,000 are approved by the DC manager. Requests above
that and up to Rs. 2 lakh are approved by Anjali Deshmukh for Finance. Anything
larger needs the Managing Director's approval.

15.4. An urgent request is marked urgent and phoned through to Finance as well
as written. Marking a routine request urgent to jump the queue is noted in the
monthly Stores report.

15.5. Stores does not accept gifts, samples or free stock from suppliers. A
supplier who sends samples is asked to take them back.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and

## 5. Instruments that travel south

5.1. Coimbatore has no calibration chamber and no bench master logger. Those
live at Nagpur. What Coimbatore does have is one lab-certified hand-held
thermometer, serial HP-C00, kept locked in the DC manager's cabinet.

5.2. Every hand-held thermometer in daily use at Coimbatore is checked against
HP-C00 every 14 days: both tips go into the same stirred jug of crushed ice and
water, and the two readings must agree within 0.5 C. The shift lead writes both
readings on QCL-F-12 and sends a photograph of the sheet to the Nagpur QA desk.

5.3. The shorter interval is deliberate. Coimbatore has no bench to catch a
drifting instrument quickly, and a second jug check costs nothing but ten
minutes.

5.4. HP-C00 itself goes to Metrosure Labs, Pune, by courier every 12 months.
While it is away, the Nagpur QA desk sends a loan instrument ahead of it, so the
site is never without a certified thermometer.

5.5. USB loggers are not checked at Coimbatore at all. Every spare logger for a
Coimbatore red sleeve is checked at the Nagpur bench and arrives in its sleeve
already stickered. A logger that has been out of date on the shelf is sent back
to Nagpur, never re-used on the strength of a local jug check.

5.6. Infrared guns are used at Coimbatore only to find a warm carton quickly.
They are never the reading that decides anything.

## Hand-held probes

1. Fill the insulated jug with crushed ice made from potable water. Top it up with cold potable water to just below the ice line and stir for 30 seconds.
2. Hold the probe tip 5 cm deep in the slurry, clear of the jug wall, for 3 minutes before you read the display.
3. The probe passes if it reads within 0.5 C of 0.0 C.
4. Repeat for every hand-held probe on the monthly list. A probe is due every 30 days.

## At the bench

7. A pass gets a green sticker with the next due date, and the reading goes on QCL-F-12 the same day.
8. A fail gets red DO NOT USE tape and goes in the blue bin at the QA desk. Do not adjust the offset yourself. QA sends failed instruments to Metrosure Labs, Pune.

## Keeping the bench tidy

Spare sticker rolls live in the top drawer. The date stamp is reset every Monday
by the day QA officer. Green tape marks the clean side of the bench, where
nothing wet is put down. Filled QCL-F-12 sheets go to the QA file room at month
end. The jug is emptied and dried at the end of every shift, and the scoop is
kept in its bag.

# Probe and logger calibration at the QA bench

Carried out at the QA bench in Nagpur by any QA officer or trained shift lead.
The bench kit is the insulated jug, the ice scoop, the calibration chamber and
the bench master logger.

## USB loggers

5. Put the logger beside the bench master in the calibration chamber at +5.0 C for 30 minutes; it passes if it reads within 0.3 C of the master.
6. Every spare logger is checked this way before it is packed into a red sleeve, whatever its sticker says.

# Probe calibration: terms and tolerances

## Terms

- **ice point** — 0.0 C, the temperature of a stirred slurry of crushed ice and potable water.
- **bench master** — the lab-certified logger kept in the QA calibration chamber at Nagpur, serial UL-M01, recertified every 12 months by Metrosure Labs.
- **drift** — the change in an instrument's error between two checks.
- **pass band** — the largest error an instrument may show and still be used.

## Instruments

| instrument | prefix | pass band | in-house check | external calibration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hand-held probe | HP- | ±0.5 C at the ice point | every 30 days | every 12 months |

## Drift

A probe that drifts more than 0.3 C between two monthly checks goes for external calibration even if it passed both.

## 7. Leaving the building in a hurry

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

## Sticker colours

- **green** — in date.
- **yellow** — check due within 7 days; the instrument may still be used.
- **red** — failed; out of use until QA clears it.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## Notes on the lab

Drift is normal in cheap probes and is the main reason the bench exists. Monthly
figures are kept on QCL-F-12 so that a trend can be seen. External labs issue
one certificate per instrument, which QA files against the prefix number. An
instrument that passed at the lab still needs its in-house check when it comes
back.

An infrared gun reads a carton surface, not the product, and is never the
reading used to release stock.

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

# Dry ice handling card, dock 5 board

Printed for the board beside dock 5, where frozen top-ups are loaded.

## Before you touch it

Cryogenic gloves and face shield from the rack beside the chest. No cotton
gloves, no bare hands.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

## Afterwards

5. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.
6. In the monsoon, keep the tote covered between the cage and the dock; rain on dry ice throws up fog that hides the dock edge.

## Frozen body top-up

5. Tote on the body floor at the rear, doors open, engine off. Nobody goes into the body for 1 minute.
6. Empty the tote into the top-up tray, then close up.

## Frozen body top-up

4. Tote on the body floor at the rear, doors open, engine off; keep out of the body until the Guwahati night lead says it is clear.

## 6. Roadside trouble

6.1. A driver whose vehicle develops a fault stops at a safe place first and
calls second. A lit fuel plaza, a toll rest area or a police post is a safe
place; a road shoulder at night is not, unless the vehicle cannot be moved.

6.2. Roadside tyre changes on a loaded reefer are done by the listed tyre
vendor, never by the driver alone, and Fleet Control expects the vendor within
3 hours on a qualified lane.

6.3. A reefer unit fault is reported with the display reading, the alarm code
and the time. Fleet Control decides whether to send the mobile service van,
transfer the load, or bring the vehicle in. The driver does not open the reefer
unit's panel.

6.4. A breakdown on a lane where the fuel pumps are a quarter of a day apart
makes the wait long. Drivers on such lanes carry water and a torch, and the
mobile service van is not always the quickest help; sometimes the relief point
vendor on the lane arrives first.

6.5. A vehicle that cannot be moved and is carrying pharma critical stock is
reported to Compliance-Red by Fleet Control within the SOP's notification
window, whatever the cause.

6.6. After any roadside repair, the vehicle is walked round again before it
moves, as if it were being taken over.

4.4. Each DC holds two bolt-seal cutters, and a lost cutter is replaced by Stores

2. Bolt seal on owned reefers, cable seal on hired trucks.
3. Record the number on the dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.
4. Photograph the seal with the dock clock in frame.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

## 13. Forms and printed stationery

13.1. Stores holds the printed pads of every QCL form used on the floor, from the
customer intimation form to the wash register. Each pad carries the form number
and the revision printed at its foot.

13.2. When QA issues a new revision of a form, Stores withdraws every pad of the
earlier revision from the DC shelves in the same week and sends the withdrawn
pads to QA to be counted and shredded. Two revisions of one form are never on a
shelf at the same time.

13.3. Forms are issued to shift leads by the pad, never by the loose sheet, so
that a used pad can be matched to the shift that used it.

13.4. Stores reorders a form when its stock falls to three months' use. The
print order goes through Finance like any other purchase.

13.5. Dispatch notes are printed with running numbers. Stores records the first
and last number of each box issued to a gate, as it does for other numbered
stock.

## 10. Counting

10.1. Stores counts seals, sleeves and instruments every Friday, and everything
else at the month end.

10.2. A count is done by two people, one of whom did not issue anything that
week.

10.3. At the Friday count the logger shelf is checked by date: a logger whose
last bench check is more than 90 days old is moved to the QA tray, and a logger
whose battery date shows more than 24 months is flagged, but nothing in the
store count replaces what the QA bench decides.

10.4. Differences are written up the same day and sent to Nalini Patil. A
difference in seals or loggers is reported to QA and Fleet Control as well.

10.5. Guwahati and Coimbatore cages send their counts to the Nagpur store by
email on the first working day of the month.

## Why pallet labels on pharma

The BharatVac audit of February 2026 asked for evidence at pallet level, not
only at the door. A tamper label across the stretch wrap shows whether a pallet
was opened between our gate and the customer's.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

# Dry ice at Quillfern: why the present rules

## Why it stays out of C2 and C3

On the night of 12 March 2025 dry ice trays were set outside the inner curtain
of C2 to hold the room down. The intention was good, but the trays masked the room reading at the curtain and put the vials nearest the door at risk of dropping below +2.0 C.
A pharma room is protected by containment and quarantine, not by cooling it from
the outside.

## Taking it out

1. Sign the pellets out on QCL-F-26 with the kg, the job and your name.
2. Scoop the pellets into an insulated tote. Never put dry ice in a sealed box, a flask or a drum with a screw lid.
3. A load above 10 kg is carried by two people.
4. Dry ice never travels in a driver's cab, and never goes into cold room C2 or C3.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
07:45 and 08:30. Drivers are told on booking to arrive either before 07:30 or
after 08:40. A reefer is never queued across Temple Street; if the apron is
full, the driver goes round the block and comes back.

3.3. Security holds each vehicle outside the south gate until the previous one
has cleared the apron. The apron takes one reefer and one van at a time, no
more, because a reversing reefer cannot see a second one parked behind it.

3.4. Bookings are made in Dockwise, which Coimbatore joined on 1 February 2026.
The grace table and the cancellation rule are the company rule, not a local
one, and are not repeated here.

3.5. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. After about 13:00 the afternoon sun
lies across the outer apron, drivers open their doors to check paperwork, and
the frozen body loses cold it cannot spare.

3.6. Reversing on the apron after dark needs a spotter with a torch, whatever
the vehicle's camera shows. The apron lights are on a timer that the landlord
controls, and they have twice failed to come on in the monsoon.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

## Why pellets

Quillfern used to buy dry ice in blocks. Blocks had to be broken with a mallet on the dock, and two hand injuries in 2024 came from exactly that.
The blocks came in 12 kg slabs, and staff carried the slabs by hand because no
tote was used for them. The chest lid has two handles. Vidarbha Gases rated
pellets as easier to meter by the kg, and pellets of 16 mm from Vidarbha Gases
replaced blocks in 2024.

## Why a second pair of hands

The tote handles are rated for 12 kg, so one person with a full tote is already at the limit of the handles.
A dropped tote on a wet dock scatters pellets that people then pick up with the
wrong gloves.

## 6. Spare instruments

6.1. Stores holds spare hand-held probes and spare USB loggers for issue, but
does not decide whether an instrument is fit to use. The sticker, put on by QA,
decides that.

6.2. A spare logger's battery is replaced by Stores after 24 months on the
shelf, whatever the logger's sticker says, and the logger then goes back to the
QA bench before it can be issued.

6.3. An instrument with a yellow sticker may be issued. An instrument with a red
sticker or red tape is never issued and goes back to QA.

6.4. Stores keeps a list of every instrument by its prefix number and the date
of its last in-house check, so that QA can see what is due.

6.5. Instruments sent to the external lab are packed by QA and handed to the
courier by Stores. Stores records the date they left and the date they came
back.

## Sticker colours

- **green** — in date.
- **yellow** — check due within 7 days; the instrument may still be used.
- **red** — failed; out of use until QA clears it.

## Hand-held probes

1. Fill the insulated jug with crushed ice made from potable water. Top it up with cold potable water to just below the ice line and stir for 30 seconds.
2. Hold the probe tip 5 cm deep in the slurry, clear of the jug wall, for 3 minutes before you read the display.
3. The probe passes if it reads within 0.5 C of 0.0 C.
4. Repeat for every hand-held probe on the monthly list. A probe is due every 30 days.

# Probe and logger calibration at the QA bench

Carried out at the QA bench in Nagpur by any QA officer or trained shift lead.
The bench kit is the insulated jug, the ice scoop, the calibration chamber and
the bench master logger.

## 1. What Stores does

1.1. Stores buys nothing on its own authority. It raises a request against a
purchase order that Finance has approved, receives the goods, holds them, issues
them against a signature and counts them.

1.2. The Nagpur main store keeps the stock for Nagpur and sends stock to
Guwahati and Coimbatore by courier or on a scheduled vehicle. The Guwahati and
Coimbatore cages hold only what their DC uses in about a month.

1.3. Every item issued is signed for by the person who takes it. An item that
leaves Stores without a signature is counted as lost at the next count.

1.4. Stores does not lend. An item taken for a job is either used, returned or
written off, and each of those is recorded.

## USB loggers

5. Put the logger beside the bench master in the calibration chamber at +5.0 C for 30 minutes; it passes if it reads within 0.3 C of the master.
6. Every spare logger is checked this way before it is packed into a red sleeve, whatever its sticker says.

## At the bench

7. A pass gets a green sticker with the next due date, and the reading goes on QCL-F-12 the same day.
8. A fail gets red DO NOT USE tape and goes in the blue bin at the QA desk. Do not adjust the offset yourself. QA sends failed instruments to Metrosure Labs, Pune.

## Keeping the bench tidy

Spare sticker rolls live in the top drawer. The date stamp is reset every Monday
by the day QA officer. Green tape marks the clean side of the bench, where
nothing wet is put down. Filled QCL-F-12 sheets go to the QA file room at month
end. The jug is emptied and dried at the end of every shift, and the scoop is
kept in its bag.

## Drift

A probe that drifts more than 0.3 C between two monthly checks goes for external calibration even if it passed both.

## Instruments

| instrument | prefix | pass band | in-house check | external calibration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hand-held probe | HP- | ±0.5 C at the ice point | every 30 days | every 12 months |

## Notes on the lab

Drift is normal in cheap probes and is the main reason the bench exists. Monthly
figures are kept on QCL-F-12 so that a trend can be seen. External labs issue
one certificate per instrument, which QA files against the prefix number. An
instrument that passed at the lab still needs its in-house check when it comes

# Probe calibration: terms and tolerances

## Terms

- **ice point** — 0.0 C, the temperature of a stirred slurry of crushed ice and potable water.
- **bench master** — the lab-certified logger kept in the QA calibration chamber at Nagpur, serial UL-M01, recertified every 12 months by Metrosure Labs.
- **drift** — the change in an instrument's error between two checks.
- **pass band** — the largest error an instrument may show and still be used.

21.4. A supplier who has had three returns in a year is raised at the annual

## 3. Receiving goods

3.1. Goods are received against the purchase order and the delivery note, and
counted before the delivery note is signed. A short delivery is written as short

3.2. Temperature-sensitive consumables, such as conditioned gel packs, are not
received by Stores. They go directly to the QA room.

3.3. Calibrated instruments are received by Stores and passed unopened to the QA
bench on the same day. Stores does not open an instrument box to check it.

3.4. Damaged goods are photographed, set aside and reported to Finance before the
supplier's driver leaves, where that is possible.

## 11. Crashes, near misses and police stops

11.1. After any crash, however small, the driver makes the vehicle and the road
safe, calls emergency services if anyone is hurt, and then calls Fleet Control.

11.2. The driver does not move the vehicle unless the police tell him to or it
is a danger where it stands. Photographs of the scene are taken if it is safe.

11.3. The driver is relieved from further driving until Fleet Control records a
fitness-to-continue decision, as the policy requires.

11.4. A near miss is reported the same day, in the driver's own words. Near-miss
reports are not used to discipline the driver who reports them.

11.5. A police stop that is not a crash and not an inspection of the load, such
as a document check, is noted in the driver call log with the time and place.

## 9. Protective equipment

9.1. Stores issues cryogenic gloves, face shields, freezer suits, safety shoes,
high-visibility vests and hearing protection against a signature.

9.2. Freezer suits are issued to named people, not to a shift. A suit that no
longer closes properly is returned and replaced.

9.3. Cryogenic gloves and face shields for dry-ice work are not personal issue.
They hang on the rack beside each chest and are replaced by Stores when damaged.

9.4. Safety shoes are replaced once a year, or sooner if the sole is split.

9.5. Hired-truck drivers are issued a high-visibility vest at the gate and return
it at the gate.

## 18. Audit of Stores

18.1. Finance audits the Nagpur store twice a year without notice, counting a
sample of lines chosen on the day.

18.2. QA audits the numbered stock once a year, from the manufacturer's delivery
note to the gate register and back to the stubs.

18.3. Findings are written up by the auditor and answered by Nalini Patil within
ten working days, with an owner and a date for each action.

18.4. A finding that repeats from one audit to the next is escalated to the
Nagpur DC manager and to Finance.

## 18. Review of this manual

18.1. The Fleet head reviews this manual every April, alongside the annual review
of the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy, and sooner after any crash or serious
exception that shows a gap in it.

18.2. Drivers and controllers send suggested changes to Fleet Control at any
time. Suggestions are read at the next Nagpur driver meeting.

18.3. A revised manual replaces every earlier copy at the Fleet Control desk, the
gate cabins and the driver rest room on the day it is issued.

## 14. Housekeeping and pests

14.1. The cold block floor is swept at the end of each shift and mopped once a
day, after the last frozen load of the morning. Mopping is never done while a
pallet is moving, because a wet floor in front of FL-C2 is how a pallet ends up
on its side.

14.2. Cardboard dust is the main dirt in the dry block. The racks S1 to S6 are
dusted on the first Saturday of the month, top shelf first, and the floor is
swept after the dusting, not before.

14.3. The pest control contractor, Kongu Hygiene Services, visits on the second
Wednesday of every month and on call after any sighting. Bait stations are
numbered on the wall plan in the office annexe. Nobody moves a bait station to
make room for stock; the contractor moves it and redraws the plan.

14.4. Birds nest in the open-sided shed and under the apron canopy. The netting
over the canopy is checked after every storm. A bird inside the cold block is
reported to the shift lead at once, and the room door is kept shut until the
contractor has taken it out.

14.5. The canteen is cleaned by the canteen contractor, not by site staff. Any
complaint about the canteen goes to the DC manager in writing.

## 7. Leaving the building in a hurry

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 22. Energy and waste in the store

22.1. The store lights are on a timer and go off at 19:30. The storekeeper
closing the store checks that the cage, the flammables cabinet and the emergency
cupboard are locked before the lights go off.

22.2. Packaging from deliveries is flattened and sent to the scrap area on the
day it arrives. The store is not a place to keep empty boxes.

22.3. Used toner cartridges are returned to the toner supplier for recycling.

22.4. Stores reports its waste once a year to the Nagpur DC manager, by type and
weight, for the site's environmental return.

## 3. Planning a week of duty

3.1. Planners build the week's duty on Thursday for the following Monday to
Sunday. Each driver's weekly rest is placed first, then night segments, then
day runs.

3.2. The limits the plan must respect are in the Driver Hours and Road Safety
Policy. A plan that meets them only if nothing goes wrong does not meet them.

3.3. A lane with a qualification record is planned with that record open, so
that its relief point, its pre-cool hold time and any two-driver condition are
on the plan and not in someone's memory.

3.4. Festival shuttle rosters with split rest are planned only after the Fleet
head has approved the roster in writing, and only for the festival named.

3.5. The plan is published to drivers by Friday noon. A driver who sees a
problem with his week tells Fleet Control on Friday, not on the morning of the
run.

3.6. Leave requests go to the planner by the 20th of the previous month. Late
leave is granted where cover exists, and cover is never found by stretching

## 6. Roadside trouble

6.1. A driver whose vehicle develops a fault stops at a safe place first and
calls second. A lit fuel plaza, a toll rest area or a police post is a safe
place; a road shoulder at night is not, unless the vehicle cannot be moved.

6.2. Roadside tyre changes on a loaded reefer are done by the listed tyre
vendor, never by the driver alone, and Fleet Control expects the vendor within
3 hours on a qualified lane.

6.3. A reefer unit fault is reported with the display reading, the alarm code
and the time. Fleet Control decides whether to send the mobile service van,
transfer the load, or bring the vehicle in. The driver does not open the reefer
unit's panel.

6.4. A breakdown on a lane where the fuel pumps are a quarter of a day apart
makes the wait long. Drivers on such lanes carry water and a torch, and the
mobile service van is not always the quickest help; sometimes the relief point
vendor on the lane arrives first.

6.5. A vehicle that cannot be moved and is carrying pharma critical stock is
reported to Compliance-Red by Fleet Control within the SOP's notification
window, whatever the cause.

6.6. After any roadside repair, the vehicle is walked round again before it
moves, as if it were being taken over.

## 12. Paperwork that comes back

12.1. Each trip returns a trip bag holding the dispatch note, the fuel slips,
the cut seals, the takeover sheet and any exception form.

12.2. The trip bag is handed to the shift lead at the returning DC, who checks
it against the dispatch note and signs for it.

12.3. A missing item in the trip bag is written on the dispatch note as
missing, never replaced with a guess. A torn fuel slip is kept torn.

12.4. Trip bags from a trip involving a tyre change or other vendor work carry
the vendor's job sheet with the hours and the spare parts used, so that Fleet
Control can match it to the vendor's invoice.

12.5. Trip bags are kept by Fleet Control for three years, or seven where the
trip involved a pharma critical excursion, a crash, an insurance claim or a
police matter.

# Gel packs and passive shippers: terms and figures

## Packs

- **blue-cap pack** — conditioned at +5.0 C; the only pack used for pharma.
- **white-cap pack** — conditioned at -20 C; frozen goods only, never in a shipper with blue-cap packs.
- **cycle** — one conditioning and one use. A pack is retired after 40 cycles; the count is kept by punching the tab on the pack.
- A pack found swollen or leaking is retired whatever its count.

# Gel packs: why blue caps, 18 hours and a cycle limit

## Why packs are conditioned at +5.0 C, not frozen

The 2025 shipper validation first used packs straight from a freezer. Three of the five trial runs dipped to +1.4 C at the carton nearest a frozen pack.
A vaccine that freezes is lost for good; a warm excursion at least has a
stability letter to argue with.

# Gel packs: making up a passive shipper for a pharma run

## Before you start

1. Open the shipper register and confirm the shipper conditioning time (SCT) entry shows 18 hours at +5.0 C completed for every pack batch in the shipper.
2. Take blue-cap packs only, from conditioning cabinet CC-1 in the Nagpur QA room.

3. Load the packs in the pattern printed inside the shipper lid, then put the product box in the middle with a USB logger taped to its side.
4. Close the lid and fix a tamper label across the lid seam.
5. Write the shipper number (PS-01 to PS-12), the pack batch and the time the lid was closed in the shipper register.

## Why a cycle limit

Every freeze and thaw works the seam of a pack. A pack that leaks inside a
shipper wets the product box and ruins the label, so packs are retired on a
count, not on how they look.

6. Never mix white-cap packs with blue-cap packs in one shipper.

## Why 18 hours

Packs pulled after 12 hours of conditioning ran warm from about hour 30 of the trial.
At 18 hours every run held range for the length of the lane.

4.1. Seals come from the seal manufacturer in books, already numbered in order.
Stores records the first and last number of each book received.

4.4. Each DC holds two bolt-seal cutters, and a lost cutter is replaced by Stores

4.5. Tamper labels for pharma pallets and shipper lids are issued in rolls of
200 to QA, not to the gate.

4.6. Seal books for Guwahati and Coimbatore go by courier, two books at a time,
and are signed for at the gate cabin on arrival.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
07:45 and 08:30. Drivers are told on booking to arrive either before 07:30 or
after 08:40. A reefer is never queued across Temple Street; if the apron is
full, the driver goes round the block and comes back.

3.3. Security holds each vehicle outside the south gate until the previous one
has cleared the apron. The apron takes one reefer and one van at a time, no
more, because a reversing reefer cannot see a second one parked behind it.

3.4. Bookings are made in Dockwise, which Coimbatore joined on 1 February 2026.
The grace table and the cancellation rule are the company rule, not a local
one, and are not repeated here.

3.5. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. After about 13:00 the afternoon sun
lies across the outer apron, drivers open their doors to check paperwork, and
the frozen body loses cold it cannot spare.

3.6. Reversing on the apron after dark needs a spotter with a torch, whatever
the vehicle's camera shows. The apron lights are on a timer that the landlord
controls, and they have twice failed to come on in the monsoon.

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## 4. Seal books

4.1. Seals come from the seal manufacturer in books, already numbered in order.
Stores records the first and last number of each book received.

4.2. Stores issues seal books to a DC gate one book at a time against the gate's

unopened books in its locked drawer; a third is not issued until one of the two
is opened.

4.3. Spoiled seals marked VOID come back to Stores with their stubs. Stores
counts the stubs against QCL-F-35 every Friday, and a number that is neither
fitted, spoiled nor on the shelf is reported to Fleet Control the same day.

4.4. Each DC holds two bolt-seal cutters, and a lost cutter is replaced by Stores
within one working day.

4.5. Tamper labels for pharma pallets and shipper lids are issued in rolls of
200 to QA, not to the gate.

4.6. Seal books for Guwahati and Coimbatore go by courier, two books at a time,
and are signed for at the gate cabin on arrival.

# Seals and tamper labels: types and codes

## Types

- **bolt seal** — a steel bolt and barrel, used once, fitted to the rear door hasp of an owned reefer. Prefix QB, six digits, for example QB-204117.
- **cable seal** — a steel cable locked through the hasp of a hired truck. Prefix QC.
- **tamper label** — an adhesive label that tears if lifted, fixed across the stretch wrap of pharma pallets and the lid seam of passive shippers. Prefix QP.

## Cost

Seal books are charged to the Fleet cost centre by Stores at issue.

## 1. What Stores does

1.1. Stores buys nothing on its own authority. It raises a request against a
purchase order that Finance has approved, receives the goods, holds them, issues
them against a signature and counts them.

1.2. The Nagpur main store keeps the stock for Nagpur and sends stock to
Guwahati and Coimbatore by courier or on a scheduled vehicle. The Guwahati and
Coimbatore cages hold only what their DC uses in about a month.

1.3. Every item issued is signed for by the person who takes it. An item that
leaves Stores without a signature is counted as lost at the next count.

1.4. Stores does not lend. An item taken for a job is either used, returned or
written off, and each of those is recorded.

## 24. Review of this standard

24.1. Nalini Patil reviews this standard every July with QA and Finance, and
sooner when a new consumable is introduced or a supplier changes.

24.2. A change to how an item is used is made in the document that governs its
use, not here. This standard changes only how Stores receives, holds, issues and
counts the item.

24.3. Each revision is issued with a note of what changed. The storekeepers at
Nagpur and the cage leads at Guwahati and Coimbatore sign that they have read it
within a week.

24.4. The earlier revision is withdrawn from the Stores counter and the shared
drive on the day the new one is issued, so that nobody works from two versions
at the same time.

## Books and register

- **seal book** — 25 seals in number order. Only one book is open at the gate at a time.
- **QCL-F-35** — the seal register; one line per seal fitted, cut or spoiled.
- **VOID** — a seal spoiled while fitting; it is cut, bagged with its stub and never reused.
- **trip bag** — the bag that travels back with the dispatch note and holds the cut seals from that trip.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

# Dry ice: properties and limits

## What it is

- **dry ice** — solid carbon dioxide. At normal pressure it turns straight into gas at -78.5 C; it does not melt into a liquid.
- **pellet** — the 16 mm form Quillfern buys from Vidarbha Gases.
- **sublimation loss** — stock that turns to gas while waiting; about 8% of the chest's contents a day with the lid shut.

## 6. Roadside trouble

6.1. A driver whose vehicle develops a fault stops at a safe place first and
calls second. A lit fuel plaza, a toll rest area or a police post is a safe
place; a road shoulder at night is not, unless the vehicle cannot be moved.

6.2. Roadside tyre changes on a loaded reefer are done by the listed tyre
vendor, never by the driver alone, and Fleet Control expects the vendor within
3 hours on a qualified lane.

6.3. A reefer unit fault is reported with the display reading, the alarm code
and the time. Fleet Control decides whether to send the mobile service van,
transfer the load, or bring the vehicle in. The driver does not open the reefer
unit's panel.

6.4. A breakdown on a lane where the fuel pumps are a quarter of a day apart
makes the wait long. Drivers on such lanes carry water and a torch, and the
mobile service van is not always the quickest help; sometimes the relief point
vendor on the lane arrives first.

6.5. A vehicle that cannot be moved and is carrying pharma critical stock is
reported to Compliance-Red by Fleet Control within the SOP's notification
window, whatever the cause.

6.6. After any roadside repair, the vehicle is walked round again before it
moves, as if it were being taken over.

## 4. Taking over a vehicle

4.1. The driver taking over a vehicle walks round it with the driver handing
over, or with the shift lead if the vehicle was parked empty.

4.2. The walk-round covers tyres and wheel nuts, lights, mirrors, the reefer
unit's display and alarm light, the rear door hasp, the cab locker and the red
sleeve, the fire extinguisher, and the wheel chocks.

4.3. Any damage found on the walk-round is photographed and written on the
takeover sheet before the vehicle moves. Damage found later is presumed to have
happened on the later driver's watch.

4.4. The cab card is checked for the current Fleet Control, QA desk and
Compliance-Red numbers. A cab card printed before the Tessaline cutover is
replaced before the vehicle leaves.

4.5. The driver checks that the Tessaline unit shows the vehicle's own asset
number. Units have been swapped between vehicles in the workshop and not
re-labelled.

## 15. Route changes and diversions

15.1. A driver does not change the planned route on his own judgement unless the
road ahead is closed or unsafe. He stops, calls Fleet Control, and follows the
diversion Fleet Control gives.

15.2. Fleet Control checks any diversion against the lane record for that trip,
because a diversion may take the vehicle through a dead zone or past no safe
stopping place.

15.3. A diversion that adds a toll, a ghat road or a city centre is written on
the dispatch note with the reason.

15.4. Customer service is told of any diversion that will change the arrival
window, and tells the customer. The driver does not tell the customer himself.

15.5. Festivals, elections and large public events close roads without much
notice. Planners check the week's public calendar on Thursday when they build
the plan, and Fleet Control checks it again each morning.

## 18. Review of this manual

18.1. The Fleet head reviews this manual every April, alongside the annual review
of the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy, and sooner after any crash or serious
exception that shows a gap in it.

18.2. Drivers and controllers send suggested changes to Fleet Control at any
time. Suggestions are read at the next Nagpur driver meeting.

18.3. A revised manual replaces every earlier copy at the Fleet Control desk, the
gate cabins and the driver rest room on the day it is issued.

## 6. After the washdown

6.1. A washed body is not loaded until it has been chilled again from empty; the dispatch checklist for the load sets how long.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

## 5. Where and who

5.1. Nagpur: the wash bay beside the generator room. Guwahati: the contract garage. Coimbatore: the wash pad inside the south gate.

5.2. The shift lead signs the wash register QCL-F-40. The driver may do the washdown but may not sign it.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

# Seals: fitting and recording them at the gate

## Fitting

1. Take the next seal in number order from the open seal book; never skip a number.
2. Owned reefers get a bolt seal on the rear door hasp; hired trucks get a cable seal.
3. Write the seal number on the dispatch note and in seal register QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.
4. Photograph the seal with the dock clock in frame.
5. A seal spoiled while fitting is cut, bagged with its stub, written VOID in QCL-F-35 and returned to Stores within 24 hours.

## Books and register

- **seal book** — 25 seals in number order. Only one book is open at the gate at a time.
- **QCL-F-35** — the seal register; one line per seal fitted, cut or spoiled.
- **VOID** — a seal spoiled while fitting; it is cut, bagged with its stub and never reused.
- **trip bag** — the bag that travels back with the dispatch note and holds the cut seals from that trip.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
