# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed temperature
excursion in Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. warehouses, docks, cross-dock
lanes, owned reefer trucks and hired trucks working under Quillfern dispatch.
The procedure applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled dairy, paneer, frozen food,
and any customer stock moved under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. The purpose is to protect patient safety, food safety, customer evidence,
and the company record. A fast release is never preferred over a complete
temperature history. Staff must treat a missing record as a quality event until
QA closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration. A single hand-held thermometer reading is not
enough to release product after a breach; it may be used only to start immediate
containment while the logger history is retrieved.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

## 3. How long stock may sit

3.1. Quarantine Dwell Limit (QDL) is the time stock may stay in quarantine after the excursion is confirmed before the account manager must escalate to the customer's quality head.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| pharma critical | 72 hours |

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 10. Closure

10.1. The QA head or nominated deputy closes pharma critical investigations. The
DC manager may close dairy and frozen investigations only after QA records the
disposition.

10.2. Corrective and preventive actions must have an owner, a due date, and
evidence of completion. "Discussed on call" is not completion evidence.

10.3. Training actions shall be assigned by role, not by name alone, so that new
staff receive the same correction.

10.4. The case file must be kept for seven years for pharma critical stock and
three years for food stock.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| dairy | 12 hours |

3.2. Reaching the QDL does not release anything. It starts an escalation; the stock stays where it is.

## 6. After the washdown

6.1. A washed body is not loaded until it has been chilled again from empty; the dispatch checklist for the load sets how long.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

# Quarantine Stock Release and Return Procedure

How stock leaves quarantine bays Q-3 (Nagpur), Q-G2 (Guwahati) and Q-C1 (Coimbatore) after QA has recorded a disposition under clause 6.5 of the [Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). Destroyed stock does not leave by this procedure; section 7 of that SOP governs it.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: what to do

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks where they are and switch the engines off. Nobody drives through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door that does not face the compressor house. The security guard brings the gate register.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register and the dock sheet within 10 minutes and phones the count to the plant operator on extension 215.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, a phone or a truck. Pallets left on a dock are dealt with afterwards under QCL-QA-SOP-17; product loss is a QA matter.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: why M2, and why nobody goes back

## Why M2 and not the canteen lawn

Until 2024 the ammonia muster point was M1, the canteen lawn. In the July 2024 monsoon drill the windsock put the canteen lawn downwind of the compressor house for four of the six drill hours.
M2, by gate 2, sits upwind under the south-west monsoon wind and has a second
way out on to the ring road. M1 is still the fire muster point.

reads below full is swapped the same day. The room itself is inspected by the

7. Stay at M2 until the plant operator gives the all clear in person or over the PA; a text message is not an all clear.
8. Drivers return to their vehicles only after the shift lead has re-counted at M2.

Nobody goes back for stock because in the 2024 drill a loader went back to dock 5 for his phone and was counted missing for 12 minutes.

## 10. Emergency cold for a customer's kitchen

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their
own freezer fails. Customer service takes the request; the DC decides whether it
can be done.

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing
can be ready, and the agent passes that on.

10.3. Emergency dry-ice packing is billed at a minimum of 10 kg per request,
whatever smaller quantity the kitchen asks for, and the per-kg price is the one
on the rate card in force.

10.4. Dry ice is never sent in a customer's own car unless the customer's driver
signs the dry-ice safety note at the gate. Customer service sends the note to
the customer with the confirmation.

10.5. Pharma customers are not offered dry-ice packing as an emergency measure.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| item | Coimbatore rule |
|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

## 4. Rooms, bays and what lives where

4.1. CBE-PHARMA is the insulin room. It holds insulin only; Coimbatore does not
store vaccines. Room limits and excursion durations are those of the SOP and
are not repeated in this handbook.

4.2. CBE-FROZEN is the freezer. It holds restaurant-chain frozen stock and a
small amount of frozen peas for a Tiruppur wholesaler.

4.3. The chilled dairy room was closed in 2024 when the Coimbatore milk account
moved to a local cooperative. Its door is still in the corridor and is labelled
CLOSED ROOM, NO STOCK. Nothing is put in it, including overflow.

4.4. Quarantine bay Q-C1 is at the north-west corner of the cold block, behind
the red chain. Only QA, through the shift lead on the phone, releases stock from
it.

4.5. Dry grocery is stored in the south block in racks S1 to S6. None of it is
cold chain, and none of it may be stacked against the cold block wall, which
sweats in the monsoon.

4.6. The battery charging bay for FL-C1 and FL-C2 is outside the cold block,
under the annexe stairs. Nobody charges a forklift inside a cold room.

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

12.1. Cardboard, stretch wrap and broken pallets are separated at the back of
the south block. A scrap dealer from Kovaipudur collects cardboard and wrap
every Tuesday and pays by the kg.

12.2. Broken pallets are stacked by the east wall for the pallet repairer, who
comes on the first working day of each month.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the
scrap pile. It is not used for anything and it is not to be sold until Finance
writes it off.

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

## 15. Customers who visit a DC

15.1. A customer who wants to visit a DC books the visit through the account
manager at least three working days ahead. The account manager tells the DC
manager and sends the customer the site's visitor rules.

15.2. Customer service does not promise a customer that they may see another
customer's stock, a quarantine bay or a cold room during a loading. The DC
manager decides what can be shown on the day.

15.3. A customer auditor's visit is handled by QA and the DC manager. Customer
service's part is to book it, send the paperwork and record the visit in the
ticket.

15.4. After a visit, the account manager asks the customer for comments in
writing within a week, and passes any comment on the site to the DC manager.

## 3. Opening an account

3.1. A new customer is opened by an account manager, never by an agent. The
account manager checks the customer's product classes against what each DC can
store and move.

3.2. A customer who needs vaccines stored at Coimbatore is told plainly that
Coimbatore does not store vaccines. A customer who needs chilled dairy stored at
Coimbatore is told the same.

3.3. A customer who wants its own pricing gets a signed annex. Until the annex
is signed, the standard rate card is the only price that may be given.

3.4. The account manager sends the customer the list of named contacts on both
sides, including who will receive an excursion notice at night.

3.5. A customer who asks to be told of every alarm, not only confirmed
excursions, is told that Quillfern notifies confirmed excursions. A customer
wanting alarm-level alerts is referred to the account manager, who may arrange a
Tessaline customer view under the annex.

## Why nobody goes back

Nobody goes back for stock because in the 2024 drill a loader went back to dock 5 for his phone and was counted missing for 12 minutes.
A missing person turns an evacuation into a search, and a search sends the plant
crew into the wrong place.

## What the drill also showed

Dock 5 is the nearest shutter to the compressor house, and it was the slowest
dock to empty. Several phones rang at once during the count and drowned out the
names, so nobody could tell at first who was missing. One trolley was left across
the dock 5 walkway, and people had to go back round it. The count is now taken
against the register and not by shouting.

## 15. Route changes and diversions

15.1. A driver does not change the planned route on his own judgement unless the
road ahead is closed or unsafe. He stops, calls Fleet Control, and follows the
diversion Fleet Control gives.

15.2. Fleet Control checks any diversion against the lane record for that trip,
because a diversion may take the vehicle through a dead zone or past no safe
stopping place.

15.3. A diversion that adds a toll, a ghat road or a city centre is written on
the dispatch note with the reason.

15.4. Customer service is told of any diversion that will change the arrival
window, and tells the customer. The driver does not tell the customer himself.

15.5. Festivals, elections and large public events close roads without much
notice. Planners check the week's public calendar on Thursday when they build
the plan, and Fleet Control checks it again each morning.

## 5. Diesel, cards and the reefer tank

5.1. Every owned reefer carries one fuel card for the truck and one for the
reefer unit, in separate sleeves. The two are billed to different cost centres
and must not be swapped.

5.2. Drivers fill only at Quillfern-listed pumps. The list is printed on the
back of the cab card and updated each quarter by Fleet Control.

5.3. A reefer unit whose fuel falls below one quarter is filled at the next
listed pump before any other stop, including a customer drop.

5.4. The truck's own tank follows the dispatch checklist at departure and is
otherwise the driver's judgement, with the rule that no vehicle is allowed to
run so low that it must stop somewhere unlit.

5.5. Fuel slips are photographed at the pump and the photograph is sent to
Fleet Control while parked. The paper slip goes into the trip bag.

5.6. A card that is refused at a listed pump is reported to Fleet Control, and
the driver waits for Fleet Control to authorise a payment. Drivers do not pay
for diesel from their own money.

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

## What the door sensor showed

The shift's Door Open Minutes (DOM) for C2 were 96, the highest recorded since Tessaline went live, because loading continued during the drill.

## Findings

1. One shift lead emailed the old qa-shared mailbox before calling Compliance-Red. The obsolete habit is named here, as clause 10.4 of the SOP requires: **qa-shared is not an escalation route.**
2. The red sleeve on RF-118 had no spare logger.
3. The night controller paused his run through [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md) when the alarm sounded; no vehicle left during the drill.
4. Two staff asked what "warm pallet" means. It is defined in [the jargon sheet](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

## 7. Leaving the building in a hurry

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

## 15. Visitors and audits

15.1. Every visitor signs the visitor book at the gate cabin and wears a visitor
badge for the whole visit. A visitor who has not signed in is not shown round,
whoever they say they are.

15.2. Customer auditors are escorted by the DC manager or a shift lead from the
gate to the gate. They may look at any room and any record they ask for, but
they do not handle stock and they do not enter a cold room without a freezer
jacket from the rack by the corridor.

15.3. Photographs inside the cold block are taken only with the DC manager's
permission, and only of the thing being audited. A customer's stock is never
photographed for another customer.

15.4. Auditors from the landlord's insurer visit once a year. They look at the
building, the fire equipment and the roof units, not at the cold chain. The DC
manager keeps the fire extinguisher service tags and the roof unit service
sheets in one folder for them.

15.5. After any audit the DC manager writes a short note of what was asked,
what was shown and what was promised, and sends it to Revathi Iyer and Farhan
Qureshi the same week. Promises made to an auditor are kept in that note, not
in anyone's memory.

15.6. School and college groups are not shown round the cold block. Requests
for such visits are passed to Pune HQ.

## 15. Customers who visit a DC

15.1. A customer who wants to visit a DC books the visit through the account
manager at least three working days ahead. The account manager tells the DC
manager and sends the customer the site's visitor rules.

15.2. Customer service does not promise a customer that they may see another
customer's stock, a quarantine bay or a cold room during a loading. The DC
manager decides what can be shown on the day.

15.3. A customer auditor's visit is handled by QA and the DC manager. Customer
service's part is to book it, send the paperwork and record the visit in the
ticket.

15.4. After a visit, the account manager asks the customer for comments in
writing within a week, and passes any comment on the site to the DC manager.

## Who do I call for a temperature alarm?

In daytime, call QA desk extension 440. At night in Nagpur, call Bunty or the
shift lead on extension 228, then Fleet Control if a truck is moving. For
patient-critical pharma, Compliance-Red is the escalation group after the 2025
drill. Please do not use the old qa-shared mailbox for urgent alarms.

## 3. Opening an account

3.1. A new customer is opened by an account manager, never by an agent. The
account manager checks the customer's product classes against what each DC can
store and move.

3.2. A customer who needs vaccines stored at Coimbatore is told plainly that
Coimbatore does not store vaccines. A customer who needs chilled dairy stored at
Coimbatore is told the same.

3.3. A customer who wants its own pricing gets a signed annex. Until the annex
is signed, the standard rate card is the only price that may be given.

3.4. The account manager sends the customer the list of named contacts on both
sides, including who will receive an excursion notice at night.

3.5. A customer who asks to be told of every alarm, not only confirmed
excursions, is told that Quillfern notifies confirmed excursions. A customer
wanting alarm-level alerts is referred to the account manager, who may arrange a
Tessaline customer view under the annex.

## 13. Records

13.1. Tickets, emails, call notes and quotations are kept in the customer
service system for three years, or seven years where the ticket concerns a
pharma critical excursion or a claim.

13.2. The agent writes what the customer said and what the agent said, not a
summary of both.

13.3. A ticket about an excursion carries the QCL-F-17 reference, so that an
auditor can move from the customer record to the QA record without asking.

13.4. Customer service's own notes on a customer's mood or manner are not kept
in the ticket. They belong in a conversation with the account manager.

## 11. Complaints and escalation

11.1. A complaint is anything a customer says is wrong with our service, even if
they do not use the word.

11.2. The agent records it, acknowledges it the same day, and passes it to the
account manager. The account manager replies within three working days.

11.3. A complaint about a driver's behaviour goes to Fleet Control and HR, not
to the driver.

11.4. A complaint that mentions safety, such as a vehicle driven fast or a
driver who looked unwell, goes to Fleet Control within the hour, whatever else
the complaint is about.

11.5. A customer who asks for a senior person is given the account manager's
name. If the account manager is away, the customer service lead takes the call.

## First day driver checklist

Bring licence, Aadhaar copy, bank details, two photos, and any vendor letter if
you are hired-truck staff. At the gate you sign the safety acknowledgement, get
the dispatch note, confirm seal numbers, and check whether the load is pharma,
dairy, frozen, or dry grocery.

Never troubleshoot a telematics device while driving. Park first. If a manager
says "just reach", call Fleet Control and ask them to record the instruction.

## What is Dockwise?

Dockwise is the slot calendar for Nagpur. TODO: ask Farhan for the link that

Nagpur late arrival goes to holding lane B, call shift lead, no automatic

C2 is the Nagpur vaccine room. F1 is the Nagpur freezer. Q-3 is Nagpur

If you do not know an acronym, ask; pretending is how audit findings are born.

## What is NGP hub?

NGP hub is Nagpur DC, our central hub. People write both names on challans and
old wiki pages. Security likes "Nagpur DC" on paper forms, but operations chat
often says "NGP hub".

7.1. The Coimbatore cold block runs on packaged refrigeration units on the roof.
There is no ammonia on this site, so the ammonia cards used at Nagpur do not
apply here and must not be pinned up here.

7.2. Coimbatore has one site siren, and it means leave the building. It sounds
for fire, for a gas smell from the canteen cylinders, and for a refrigerant leak
alarm from a roof unit.

7.3. Everyone goes to assembly point CM-1, the coconut grove corner inside the
east gate. Nobody gathers on the south apron: that is where the fire tender
comes in.

7.4. The shift lead counts against the gate register and the Dockwise day list,
and phones the count to the DC manager. Drivers waiting outside the south gate
stay outside and are counted by the guard.

7.5. Nobody goes back into the cold block for stock. Pallets left outside a room
are dealt with afterwards under the SOP.

7.6. The all clear is given in person by the DC manager or, at night, by the
senior guard after the fire service leaves.

## 14. Training and coaching for drivers

14.1. Every new owned-reefer driver rides two supervised runs with an experienced
driver before driving alone. One of the two is a night run.

14.2. The supervised runs cover the cab card, the takeover walk-round, the seal
routine, the red sleeve, the gate checklist for pharma runs and the way to speak
to Fleet Control on the phone. The experienced driver signs the new driver's
training sheet at the end of each run.

14.3. Telematics coaching calls are held within two working days of an alert, as
the policy says. The coach asks what happened before saying anything about what
should have happened.

14.4. Drivers who complete a year with no safety non-conformance receive a
certificate from the Fleet head, presented at the Nagpur driver meeting. The
certificate carries no money and is not tied to arrival times.

14.5. The Nagpur driver meeting is held on the last Saturday of each month in
the driver rest room. Attendance is paid duty time. Drivers on the road that day
receive the notes on their phone.

## At the gate

5. A test alarm is sent to Compliance-Red from the vehicle's Tessaline unit, and the QA night phone confirms receipt before the seal goes on.

6. If the Tessaline unit has not reported for 5 consecutive minutes, the vehicle does not leave.

7. Diesel is at least three-quarters of a tank, and the reefer unit's own fuel tank is full.

8. The seal is photographed with the dock clock in frame.

## 3. Planning a week of duty

3.1. Planners build the week's duty on Thursday for the following Monday to
Sunday. Each driver's weekly rest is placed first, then night segments, then
day runs.

3.2. The limits the plan must respect are in the Driver Hours and Road Safety
Policy. A plan that meets them only if nothing goes wrong does not meet them.

3.3. A lane with a qualification record is planned with that record open, so
that its relief point, its pre-cool hold time and any two-driver condition are
on the plan and not in someone's memory.

3.4. Festival shuttle rosters with split rest are planned only after the Fleet
head has approved the roster in writing, and only for the festival named.

3.5. The plan is published to drivers by Friday noon. A driver who sees a
problem with his week tells Fleet Control on Friday, not on the morning of the
run.

3.6. Leave requests go to the planner by the 20th of the previous month. Late
leave is granted where cover exists, and cover is never found by stretching
another driver's hours.

# Pharma Critical Night Dispatch Checklist

Worked through at the gate by the Fleet controller and the shift lead together before any pharma critical vehicle leaves a Quillfern DC between 22:00 and 05:00. Both sign. One signature is not a dispatch.

## 5. Diesel, cards and the reefer tank

5.1. Every owned reefer carries one fuel card for the truck and one for the
reefer unit, in separate sleeves. The two are billed to different cost centres
and must not be swapped.

5.2. Drivers fill only at Quillfern-listed pumps. The list is printed on the
back of the cab card and updated each quarter by Fleet Control.

5.3. A reefer unit whose fuel falls below one quarter is filled at the next

5.4. The truck's own tank follows the dispatch checklist at departure and is

5.5. Fuel slips are photographed at the pump and the photograph is sent to

5.6. A card that is refused at a listed pump is reported to Fleet Control, and

# Dry ice at Quillfern: why the present rules

## Why it stays out of C2 and C3

On the night of 12 March 2025 dry ice trays were set outside the inner curtain
of C2 to hold the room down. The intention was good, but the trays masked the room reading at the curtain and put the vials nearest the door at risk of dropping below +2.0 C.
A pharma room is protected by containment and quarantine, not by cooling it from
the outside.

## Root cause

The immediate cause was warm air ingress through a torn door curtain and door
opening during dairy cross-dock spillover. The deeper cause was that the Kalpa
alert routing still pointed to the old qa-shared mailbox, which was not watched
by the night team. The shift lead tried to protect the room by placing dry ice
near the curtain, but the team did not quarantine stock until the manager was
awake.

We also found that dock scheduling pushed paneer loading next to the vaccine
cold-room door. This did not create the torn curtain, but it increased door
traffic during the vulnerable period. The dock plan must separate pharma
loading from dairy overflow during night shift.

## Why pellets

Quillfern used to buy dry ice in blocks. Blocks had to be broken with a mallet on the dock, and two hand injuries in 2024 came from exactly that.
The blocks came in 12 kg slabs, and staff carried the slabs by hand because no
tote was used for them. The chest lid has two handles. Vidarbha Gases rated
pellets as easier to meter by the kg, and pellets of 16 mm from Vidarbha Gases
replaced blocks in 2024.

## 10. Training and drills

10.1. Every warehouse shift lead, fleet controller, and customer service agent
who handles cold-chain accounts must complete excursion training once each
calendar year. New joiners must complete the same training before they are
assigned unsupervised night duty.

10.2. Nagpur shall run one night-shift drill every quarter because it is the
central hub and handles the largest mix of pharma, dairy, and frozen movements.
Guwahati and Coimbatore shall each run at least two drills per year. A drill
must include one missing-record problem, not only a simple high-temperature
alarm.

10.3. Training records must show attendance, scenario, trainer, questions raised
by staff, and any local confusion found during the drill. Repeating a slide deck
without recording staff questions is not enough evidence for this SOP.

10.4. If a drill finds that staff are using a shortcut, hiding an alarm, calling
the wrong group, or relying on an obsolete document, QA must open a corrective
action. The corrective action may be simple, but it must name the obsolete habit
plainly.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

thermometer, serial HP-C00, kept locked in the DC manager's cabinet.

5.2. Every hand-held thermometer in daily use at Coimbatore is checked against
HP-C00 every 14 days: both tips go into the same stirred jug of crushed ice and
water, and the two readings must agree within 0.5 C. The shift lead writes both
readings on QCL-F-12 and sends a photograph of the sheet to the Nagpur QA desk.

5.3. The shorter interval is deliberate. Coimbatore has no bench to catch a
drifting instrument quickly, and a second jug check costs nothing but ten
minutes.

5.4. HP-C00 itself goes to Metrosure Labs, Pune, by courier every 12 months.
While it is away, the Nagpur QA desk sends a loan instrument ahead of it, so the
site is never without a certified thermometer.

5.5. USB loggers are not checked at Coimbatore at all. Every spare logger for a
Coimbatore red sleeve is checked at the Nagpur bench and arrives in its sleeve
already stickered. A logger that has been out of date on the shelf is sent back
to Nagpur, never re-used on the strength of a local jug check.

5.6. Infrared guns are used at Coimbatore only to find a warm carton quickly.
They are never the reading that decides anything.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.

## 12. Customer loggers

12.1. Some customers send their own logger with the stock. The logger travels
with the stock from the moment it arrives until it leaves.

12.2. A customer logger does not overrule the Tessaline record. If the customer
quotes their logger in an argument, the agent says that QA will compare the two
files and explain any difference.

12.3. A customer logger sent back to the customer goes with the return challan,
never by separate post.

12.4. The agent never downloads or opens a customer logger. That is QA's work.

## 3. Opening an account

3.1. A new customer is opened by an account manager, never by an agent. The
account manager checks the customer's product classes against what each DC can
store and move.

3.2. A customer who needs vaccines stored at Coimbatore is told plainly that
Coimbatore does not store vaccines. A customer who needs chilled dairy stored at
Coimbatore is told the same.

3.3. A customer who wants its own pricing gets a signed annex. Until the annex
is signed, the standard rate card is the only price that may be given.

3.4. The account manager sends the customer the list of named contacts on both
sides, including who will receive an excursion notice at night.

3.5. A customer who asks to be told of every alarm, not only confirmed
excursions, is told that Quillfern notifies confirmed excursions. A customer
wanting alarm-level alerts is referred to the account manager, who may arrange a
Tessaline customer view under the annex.

## 21. Returns to suppliers

21.1. Faulty goods are returned to the supplier with a return note on the
supplier's own form where the supplier has one, and on QCL-F-45 where it does
not.

21.2. Stores keeps a copy of every return note and follows up any return that
has not been credited or replaced within thirty days.

21.3. Returned numbered stock is listed by number on the return note, so that the
numbers can never reappear on a Quillfern shelf.

21.4. A supplier who has had three returns in a year is raised at the annual
supplier review, whatever the reason for the returns.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| item | Coimbatore rule |
|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks, engines off. Do not drive through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door away from the compressor house.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register within 15 minutes and rings the plant operator on extension 251 with the count.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, phones or trucks.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: what to do

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks where they are and switch the engines off. Nobody drives through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door that does not face the compressor house. The security guard brings the gate register.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register and the dock sheet within 10 minutes and phones the count to the plant operator on extension 215.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, a phone or a truck. Pallets left on a dock are dealt with afterwards under QCL-QA-SOP-17; product loss is a QA matter.

## Going back

7. Stay at M2 until the plant operator gives the all clear in person or over the PA; a text message is not an all clear.
8. Drivers return to their vehicles only after the shift lead has re-counted at M2.

## The compressor house

6. Only the plant crew enter the compressor house, wearing the breathing sets kept in the plant room.

## 11. Crashes, near misses and police stops

11.1. After any crash, however small, the driver makes the vehicle and the road
safe, calls emergency services if anyone is hurt, and then calls Fleet Control.

11.2. The driver does not move the vehicle unless the police tell him to or it
is a danger where it stands. Photographs of the scene are taken if it is safe.

11.3. The driver is relieved from further driving until Fleet Control records a
fitness-to-continue decision, as the policy requires.

11.4. A near miss is reported the same day, in the driver's own words. Near-miss
reports are not used to discipline the driver who reports them.

11.5. A police stop that is not a crash and not an inspection of the load, such
as a document check, is noted in the driver call log with the time and place.

# Fleet Operations Manual

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

## 9. Insulated boxes in the load

9.1. A validated passive shipper carries pharma stock inside a reefer body or on
a body without a cradle, such as RF-119.

9.2. A closed shipper is validated for 48 hours from the lid-closing time
written in the shipper register. A shipper that will still be on the road at 40
hours is called in to Fleet Control, and QA decides whether it is re-packed or
the consignment is held.

9.3. The shipper's lid is never opened on the road. The tamper label across the
lid seam is photographed at departure and again at delivery.

9.4. Shippers travel upright, strapped to the body wall, and never under other
freight.

9.5. The empty shipper comes back on the return run in the same condition it
went out, with its packs inside and its logger taped in place, so that QA can
download the logger and count the pack cycles.

## 2. The Fleet Control desk

2.1. Fleet Control sits at Nagpur DC and answers extension 301 at all hours. At
night one controller is on duty, with the Fleet head's deputy on call.

2.2. Fleet Control owns the dispatch note, the vehicle's route and the driver's
duty plan. A shift lead can hold a vehicle at the gate, but only Fleet Control
can change a route or a driver.

2.3. Every call from a driver is logged in the driver call log with the time,
the place and what was said, including calls that come to nothing. The paper
log is kept alongside the Tessaline record because network coverage is patchy
on several lanes.

2.4. Fleet Control does not pass customer pressure to a driver. A customer who
wants a location or an arrival time asks customer service, and customer service
asks Fleet Control.

2.5. Each controller hands over at 08:00 and 20:00, with every open exception,
every vehicle on the road with a pharma critical load, and every vehicle off
road for repair named aloud.

## The compressor house

6. Plant crew only, with breathing sets.

## 12. Paperwork that comes back

12.1. Each trip returns a trip bag holding the dispatch note, the fuel slips,
the cut seals, the takeover sheet and any exception form.

12.2. The trip bag is handed to the shift lead at the returning DC, who checks
it against the dispatch note and signs for it.

12.3. A missing item in the trip bag is written on the dispatch note as
missing, never replaced with a guess. A torn fuel slip is kept torn.

12.4. Trip bags from a trip involving a tyre change or other vendor work carry
the vendor's job sheet with the hours and the spare parts used, so that Fleet
Control can match it to the vendor's invoice.

12.5. Trip bags are kept by Fleet Control for three years, or seven where the
trip involved a pharma critical excursion, a crash, an insurance claim or a
police matter.

## Books and register

- **seal book** — 25 seals in number order. Only one book is open at the gate at a time.
- **QCL-F-35** — the seal register; one line per seal fitted, cut or spoiled.
- **VOID** — a seal spoiled while fitting; it is cut, bagged with its stub and never reused.
- **trip bag** — the bag that travels back with the dispatch note and holds the cut seals from that trip.

## At the destination

6. The receiver reads the number before cutting; a mismatch or a broken seal is photographed and Fleet Control is called on extension 301 before the doors open.
7. Cut seals from a completed trip are kept in the trip bag for 30 days.

## 7. When the doors are opened on the road

7.1. Police, excise, sales tax and transport officers may stop a loaded reefer
and ask to see the load. Drivers cooperate, and do not argue about cold chain
at the roadside.

7.2. The driver asks for the officer's name and badge number and writes both on
the back of the dispatch note, with the time and place. The driver photographs
the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

# Seals: fitting and recording them at the gate

## Fitting

1. Take the next seal in number order from the open seal book; never skip a number.
2. Owned reefers get a bolt seal on the rear door hasp; hired trucks get a cable seal.
3. Write the seal number on the dispatch note and in seal register QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.
4. Photograph the seal with the dock clock in frame.
5. A seal spoiled while fitting is cut, bagged with its stub, written VOID in QCL-F-35 and returned to Stores within 24 hours.

## Decision

Okapi Frozen Logistics will move to Ostrelle Telematics for 48 months. The migration
and onboarding charge is Rs. 9.21 lakh. The
recurring charge is Rs. 1048 per active truck per month and
Rs. 302 per fixed sensor per month.

No split-vendor model will be used. One support desk, one monthly export.

## Decision

Quillfern will renew Kalpa Fleet Systems for 36 months beginning 1 January 2024.
The renewal covers 147 owned reefers, 63 hired-truck devices during peak months,
and 38 fixed sensors across rooms and docks. The implementation and renewal
charge is Rs. 18.40 lakh. The recurring charge is Rs. 920 per active truck per
month and Rs. 310 per fixed sensor per month.

No split-vendor model will be used in 2024. IT will keep one support desk and
one monthly export from Kalpa. Fleet and QA will continue to use the KLP trip
number for audit packets.

## Decision

Norvell will renew Northgate Track for 48 months beginning 1 April 2022. The
renewal charge is Rs. 9.60 lakh. The recurring charge is Rs. 780 per active
truck per month and Rs. 240 per fixed sensor per month.

No split-vendor model will be used. IT keeps one support desk and one monthly
export. Fleet and Quality continue to use the NG trip number for audit packets.

## Context

Quillfern operates owned reefers, hired peak-season reefers, cold-room probes,
and dock sensors. The current vendor, Kalpa Fleet Systems, has been in use since
2014. The 2023 contract expires on 31 December 2023. Finance asked whether we
should renew Kalpa, move to Tessaline Telematics, or buy a mixed package with
truck devices from one supplier and warehouse sensors from another.

The operating requirement is simple: Fleet Control must see truck location,
temperature, door status, and alert history without calling the driver. QA must
retrieve a trip or room report during an investigation. The vendor must support
Nagpur as central hub, Guwahati and Coimbatore as smaller DCs, and hired trucks
during vaccine and dairy peak months.

## Reasons

Kalpa has local service staff within Nagpur city limits and has historically
replaced failed truck devices within one working day. The Nagpur base station is
already mounted and wired. Driver training material, customer report templates,
and the QA audit binder already use Kalpa screenshots. Switching all material
before vaccine season would create training risk.

The Kalpa quote is lower than Tessaline's first commercial quote. Tessaline
quoted Rs. 31.20 lakh for migration, device replacement, and API onboarding.
Tessaline also proposed 60-second polling and a richer API, but the API was not
available for our trial vehicles. Kalpa's five-minute polling is not ideal, but
it is known and accepted by current customer annexes.

The exit clause for Kalpa is acceptable only at contract end. Leaving early
would require six months of minimum recurring charges. This is not justified on
the evidence available in November 2023.

# Telematics vendor decision — Okapi 2023

## Context

Okapi Frozen Logistics runs 184 owned reefers, 69 hired
devices during peak months and 34 fixed sensors across rooms
and docks at Mysuru and its satellite sites. The current contract expires this
December.

## Rejected options

Tessaline was rejected in 2023 because the API was not demonstrated on a live
Quillfern route, the commercial proposal required a larger first-year payment,
and the field-support rota for Nagpur was still being hired. The evaluation team
liked the one-minute polling and the proposed exception export, but decided that
those benefits were not enough to justify a complete change before the 2024
vaccine season.

A split model was also rejected. In that model, Kalpa would have stayed on
trucks while warehouse probes moved to Tessaline. IT objected that two source
systems would create audit confusion and double monthly reconciliation work.
Finance objected that the split model removed volume discounts from both
vendors.

## 8. Carbon dioxide on board

8.1. Dry ice may be put into a frozen body only at a Quillfern DC dock or in a
customer's secure yard with Fleet Control's approval. No dry ice is added to a
body between DCs, at a relief point, at a toll plaza or at a fuel stop.

8.2. A frozen body running warm on the road is driven to the nearest Quillfern
DC or approved customer yard, within the driver's remaining hours, and the load
is protected there.

8.3. Dry ice never travels in the cab, whatever the distance. A driver who is
handed pellets for the cab refuses them.

8.4. A driver who opens a body in which dry ice has been placed stands back from
the open doors and keeps others back until the air has cleared.

8.5. Dry ice put into a body at a dock is written on the dispatch note with the
kg, so that the receiver knows to open the doors with care.

## 10. Emergency cold for a customer's kitchen

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their
own freezer fails. Customer service takes the request; the DC decides whether it
can be done.

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing
can be ready, and the agent passes that on.

10.3. Emergency dry-ice packing is billed at a minimum of 10 kg per request,
whatever smaller quantity the kitchen asks for, and the per-kg price is the one
on the rate card in force.

10.4. Dry ice is never sent in a customer's own car unless the customer's driver
signs the dry-ice safety note at the gate. Customer service sends the note to
the customer with the confirmation.

10.5. Pharma customers are not offered dry-ice packing as an emergency measure.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
07:45 and 08:30. Drivers are told on booking to arrive either before 07:30 or
after 08:40. A reefer is never queued across Temple Street; if the apron is
full, the driver goes round the block and comes back.

3.3. Security holds each vehicle outside the south gate until the previous one
has cleared the apron. The apron takes one reefer and one van at a time, no
more, because a reversing reefer cannot see a second one parked behind it.

3.4. Bookings are made in Dockwise, which Coimbatore joined on 1 February 2026.
The grace table and the cancellation rule are the company rule, not a local
one, and are not repeated here.

3.5. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. After about 13:00 the afternoon sun
lies across the outer apron, drivers open their doors to check paperwork, and
the frozen body loses cold it cannot spare.

3.6. Reversing on the apron after dark needs a spotter with a torch, whatever
the vehicle's camera shows. The apron lights are on a timer that the landlord
controls, and they have twice failed to come on in the monsoon.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| item | Coimbatore rule |
|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

6.4. The two-person figure is lower at Coimbatore than elsewhere because the
path from the shed to the apron crosses the wash pad, which is wet for most of
the day.

6.5. Dry ice never goes into CBE-PHARMA, never into the closed dairy room, and
never into a cab. Unused pellets go back to the chest in the same shift.

# Customer Service Handbook

For customer service agents and account managers at Pune HQ and at the three

those are in the SOP, the customer notification matrix and the rate card, and an

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules

wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 6. Spare instruments

6.1. Stores holds spare hand-held probes and spare USB loggers for issue, but
does not decide whether an instrument is fit to use. The sticker, put on by QA,
decides that.

6.2. A spare logger's battery is replaced by Stores after 24 months on the
shelf, whatever the logger's sticker says, and the logger then goes back to the
QA bench before it can be issued.

6.3. An instrument with a yellow sticker may be issued. An instrument with a red
sticker or red tape is never issued and goes back to QA.

6.4. Stores keeps a list of every instrument by its prefix number and the date
of its last in-house check, so that QA can see what is due.

6.5. Instruments sent to the external lab are packed by QA and handed to the
courier by Stores. Stores records the date they left and the date they came
back.

## 10. Counting

10.1. Stores counts seals, sleeves and instruments every Friday, and everything
else at the month end.

10.2. A count is done by two people, one of whom did not issue anything that
week.

10.3. At the Friday count the logger shelf is checked by date: a logger whose
last bench check is more than 90 days old is moved to the QA tray, and a logger
whose battery date shows more than 24 months is flagged, but nothing in the
store count replaces what the QA bench decides.

10.4. Differences are written up the same day and sent to Nalini Patil. A
difference in seals or loggers is reported to QA and Fleet Control as well.

10.5. Guwahati and Coimbatore cages send their counts to the Nagpur store by
email on the first working day of the month.

## Leaver

Accounts are disabled on the last working day, not at the end of the notice
period. Shared guard-cabin tablets are re-paired the same week, because a shared
device keeps a session alive long after the person has gone.

## 5. Instruments that travel south

5.1. Coimbatore has no calibration chamber and no bench master logger. Those
live at Nagpur. What Coimbatore does have is one lab-certified hand-held
thermometer, serial HP-C00, kept locked in the DC manager's cabinet.

5.2. Every hand-held thermometer in daily use at Coimbatore is checked against
HP-C00 every 14 days: both tips go into the same stirred jug of crushed ice and
water, and the two readings must agree within 0.5 C. The shift lead writes both
readings on QCL-F-12 and sends a photograph of the sheet to the Nagpur QA desk.

5.3. The shorter interval is deliberate. Coimbatore has no bench to catch a
drifting instrument quickly, and a second jug check costs nothing but ten
minutes.

5.4. HP-C00 itself goes to Metrosure Labs, Pune, by courier every 12 months.
While it is away, the Nagpur QA desk sends a loan instrument ahead of it, so the
site is never without a certified thermometer.

5.5. USB loggers are not checked at Coimbatore at all. Every spare logger for a
Coimbatore red sleeve is checked at the Nagpur bench and arrives in its sleeve
already stickered. A logger that has been out of date on the shelf is sent back
to Nagpur, never re-used on the strength of a local jug check.

5.6. Infrared guns are used at Coimbatore only to find a warm carton quickly.
They are never the reading that decides anything.

## 13. Language and new people

13.1. Coimbatore works in Tamil. Training is given by a trainer in Tamil, with
English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not

The tote handles are rated for 12 kg, so one person with a full tote is already at the limit of the handles.

## Why pellets

Quillfern used to buy dry ice in blocks. Blocks had to be broken with a mallet on the dock, and two hand injuries in 2024 came from exactly that.
The blocks came in 12 kg slabs, and staff carried the slabs by hand because no
tote was used for them. The chest lid has two handles. Vidarbha Gases rated
pellets as easier to meter by the kg, and pellets of 16 mm from Vidarbha Gases
replaced blocks in 2024.

# Dry ice at Quillfern: why the present rules

## Why it stays out of C2 and C3

On the night of 12 March 2025 dry ice trays were set outside the inner curtain
of C2 to hold the room down. The intention was good, but the trays masked the room reading at the curtain and put the vials nearest the door at risk of dropping below +2.0 C.
A pharma room is protected by containment and quarantine, not by cooling it from
the outside.

## Why the monitor over the chest

In 2024 a loader felt dizzy after the chest had been left open overnight in the
closed store. The monitor was fitted over the chest that month, so that nobody
has to judge the air by how they feel.

## 2. Daily limits

2.1. No driver shall be planned for more than 12 hours on duty in a duty day.
The driving component inside that duty day shall not exceed 9 hours.

2.2. No driver shall drive for more than 4 hours and 30 minutes continuously
without a break of at least 30 minutes. Loading supervision does not count as
the break if the driver is responsible for vehicle movement or seal watching.

2.3. Night driving between 22:00 and 05:00 shall not exceed 6 hours for a
single-driver vehicle. A two-driver vehicle may cover the night segment only if
both drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure.

2.4. A minimum rest period of 11 consecutive hours is required between duty
days. Sleeping in the driver's seat while waiting for a dock is not counted as
the 11-hour rest unless Fleet Control has released the driver and the vehicle is
parked in a safe rest location.

2.5. Every driver must receive one 24-hour weekly rest period in each rolling
seven-day period. Fleet Control shall plan the rest, not discover the breach
after payroll.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

email on the first working day of the month.

write-off sheet.

calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written

## If the monitor beeps

If the CO2 monitor over the chest beeps, leave the room, shut the door and call the shift lead.

## Why the monitor over the chest

In 2024 a loader felt dizzy after the chest had been left open overnight in the
closed store. The monitor was fitted over the chest that month, so that nobody
has to judge the air by how they feel.

## 6. The shed by the wash pad

6.1. Coimbatore buys dry ice for two jobs only: emergency packing for a
restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that
has to wait on the apron.

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,
not inside any building. The shed has a roof and no walls on two sides, so
carbon dioxide does not collect there the way it does in a closed store. For
that reason there is no carbon dioxide monitor at Coimbatore. The chest is never
moved indoors, even in heavy rain.

6.3. Supply and handling at Coimbatore:

| item | Coimbatore rule |
|---|---|
| supplier | Kovai Industrial Gases fills the chest with 60 kg every Tuesday |

## 8. North-east monsoon and the afternoon sun

8.1. Coimbatore's heavy rain comes with the north-east monsoon, from October to
December, not in the June to September months that set the calendar at Nagpur
and Guwahati.

8.2. Rain cover over rear pallets is used at Coimbatore from October to December
whenever it is raining on the apron. The site owns six tarpaulins for this.

8.3. Coimbatore does not bill the customer for rain cover. The monsoon handling
line on the rate card is a Guwahati charge and is not quoted for Coimbatore
loads. Customer service agents who copy the Guwahati line onto a Coimbatore
quotation create a credit note later.

8.4. The hot months are March to May. In those months the afternoon rule in
section 3.5 is enforced strictly, and the wash pad is used before 11:00 so that
washed bodies are not left drying in the midday sun with their doors open.

8.5. The cold block wall sweats in the monsoon. Anything stored against it on
the dry side is moved 30 cm away from the wall from October onwards.

# Dry ice handling at Nagpur stores and docks

## Before you touch it

Wear cryogenic gloves and the face shield from the rack beside the chest; cotton gloves and bare hands are never acceptable.

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

12.1. Cardboard, stretch wrap and broken pallets are separated at the back of
the south block. A scrap dealer from Kovaipudur collects cardboard and wrap
every Tuesday and pays by the kg.

12.2. Broken pallets are stacked by the east wall for the pallet repairer, who
comes on the first working day of each month.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the
scrap pile. It is not used for anything and it is not to be sold until Finance
writes it off.

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

Blue caps and white caps were chosen because the night team works under one tube light and colour is read faster than a label.

# Gel pack and shipper figures, QA room sheet

Pinned beside conditioning cabinet CC-1.

## Packs

- blue-cap pack — conditioned at +5.0 C, pharma only.
- white-cap pack — conditioned at -20 C, frozen goods only; never mixed with blue caps.
- A pack is retired after 60 cycles.

## Never

6. Never mix white-cap packs with blue-cap packs in one shipper.
7. Never put a pack straight from CC-1 against a vaccine carton without the product box between them.

## Making it up

3. Load the packs in the pattern printed inside the shipper lid, then put the product box in the middle with a USB logger taped to its side.
4. Close the lid and fix a tamper label across the lid seam.
5. Write the shipper number (PS-01 to PS-12), the pack batch and the time the lid was closed in the shipper register.

## Notes from the trial

The trial ran in the night team's slot, because that is when pharma shippers are
made up. White packs from the freezer and blue packs from CC-1 sat on separate
trolleys. One tube light over the bench had failed and was not replaced for a
week. The caps were ordered from the same supplier as the pack bodies.

# Gel packs: why blue caps, 18 hours and a cycle limit

## Why packs are conditioned at +5.0 C, not frozen

The 2025 shipper validation first used packs straight from a freezer. Three of the five trial runs dipped to +1.4 C at the carton nearest a frozen pack.
A vaccine that freezes is lost for good; a warm excursion at least has a
stability letter to argue with.

# Gel packs: making up a passive shipper for a pharma run

## Before you start

1. Open the shipper register and confirm the shipper conditioning time (SCT) entry shows 18 hours at +5.0 C completed for every pack batch in the shipper.
2. Take blue-cap packs only, from conditioning cabinet CC-1 in the Nagpur QA room.

## Shippers

- 18 blue-cap packs go in each shipper.
- Shipper conditioning time: 18 hours at +5.0 C.
- A closed shipper holds its range for 72 hours.

## Why a cycle limit

Every freeze and thaw works the seam of a pack. A pack that leaks inside a
shipper wets the product box and ruins the label, so packs are retired on a
count, not on how they look.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
07:45 and 08:30. Drivers are told on booking to arrive either before 07:30 or
after 08:40. A reefer is never queued across Temple Street; if the apron is
full, the driver goes round the block and comes back.

3.3. Security holds each vehicle outside the south gate until the previous one
has cleared the apron. The apron takes one reefer and one van at a time, no
more, because a reversing reefer cannot see a second one parked behind it.

3.4. Bookings are made in Dockwise, which Coimbatore joined on 1 February 2026.
The grace table and the cancellation rule are the company rule, not a local
one, and are not repeated here.

3.5. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. After about 13:00 the afternoon sun
lies across the outer apron, drivers open their doors to check paperwork, and
the frozen body loses cold it cannot spare.

3.6. Reversing on the apron after dark needs a spotter with a torch, whatever
the vehicle's camera shows. The apron lights are on a timer that the landlord
controls, and they have twice failed to come on in the monsoon.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

# Fleet Operations Manual

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 12. Paperwork that comes back

12.1. Each trip returns a trip bag holding the dispatch note, the fuel slips,
the cut seals, the takeover sheet and any exception form.

12.2. The trip bag is handed to the shift lead at the returning DC, who checks
it against the dispatch note and signs for it.

12.3. A missing item in the trip bag is written on the dispatch note as
missing, never replaced with a guess. A torn fuel slip is kept torn.

12.4. Trip bags from a trip involving a tyre change or other vendor work carry
the vendor's job sheet with the hours and the spare parts used, so that Fleet
Control can match it to the vendor's invoice.

12.5. Trip bags are kept by Fleet Control for three years, or seven where the
trip involved a pharma critical excursion, a crash, an insurance claim or a
police matter.

## 2. The Fleet Control desk

2.1. Fleet Control sits at Nagpur DC and answers extension 301 at all hours. At
night one controller is on duty, with the Fleet head's deputy on call.

2.2. Fleet Control owns the dispatch note, the vehicle's route and the driver's
duty plan. A shift lead can hold a vehicle at the gate, but only Fleet Control
can change a route or a driver.

2.3. Every call from a driver is logged in the driver call log with the time,
the place and what was said, including calls that come to nothing. The paper
log is kept alongside the Tessaline record because network coverage is patchy
on several lanes.

2.4. Fleet Control does not pass customer pressure to a driver. A customer who
wants a location or an arrival time asks customer service, and customer service
asks Fleet Control.

2.5. Each controller hands over at 08:00 and 20:00, with every open exception,
every vehicle on the road with a pharma critical load, and every vehicle off
road for repair named aloud.

## Why M2 and not the canteen lawn

Until 2024 the ammonia muster point was M1, the canteen lawn. In the July 2024 monsoon drill the windsock put the canteen lawn downwind of the compressor house for four of the six drill hours.
M2, by gate 2, sits upwind under the south-west monsoon wind and has a second
way out on to the ring road. M1 is still the fire muster point.

# Ammonia alarm card, canteen notice board

1. Stop forklifts and trucks, engines off. Do not drive through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door away from the compressor house.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register within 15 minutes and rings the plant operator on extension 251 with the count.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, phones or trucks.

# Ammonia plant at Nagpur: levels, places and kit

## Alarm levels

- about 5 ppm — the smell is noticeable; not an alarm.
- Stage 1 — 25 ppm at any plant-room detector: amber beacon, the plant crew investigate, and dock 5 stops loading.
- Stage 2 — 150 ppm at any detector: site siren and full evacuation to M2.
- 300 ppm — immediately dangerous to life or health; nobody without a breathing set is anywhere near it.

## 9. Insulin without spare cold

9.1. Coimbatore holds no passive shippers, no gel packs and no conditioning
cabinet. The passive shipper pilot is at Nagpur only, and it does not extend to
Coimbatore until a later project is approved.

9.2. Because there are no shippers, insulin at Coimbatore is never staged on an
open dock beyond the SOP limit. Insulin moves from CBE-PHARMA straight into a
reefer body that is already at loading temperature, and the reefer waits for
the insulin, never the other way round.

9.3. A customer who asks Coimbatore for a shipper-packed consignment is told
that the site cannot pack one. The account manager may arrange for a
shipper-packed consignment to come from Nagpur.

9.4. Coimbatore does not stock blue-cap or white-cap packs of any kind, and does
not freeze packs in CBE-FROZEN for customers. A customer's own packs returned
with a consignment go back with the customer's return challan.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

## Half two: passive shippers

Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock beyond a short limit unless a
validated passive shipper is used; the limit and the exception are clause 8.2 of
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md).

Quillfern has been refusing bookings it could have taken, including chilled
pharma on [RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md), which has no shipper cradle
and therefore cannot take pharma critical stock without one. The pilot puts
twelve validated passive shippers at Nagpur from August 2026.

Hire is charged to the customer per shipper per trip at the rate printed on
[the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md). Finance added that line to the
card when this project was approved, so the card and the project were signed in
the same week.

## 5. Taking a booking

5.1. A booking needs the product class, the quantity in the unit the rate card
uses, the pickup and delivery points, the earliest and latest delivery time, and
the name of the person who will receive.

5.2. The agent checks that the booked vehicle can carry the product class. RF-120
is frozen only; RF-119 takes pharma only with a passive shipper; RF-118 takes
pharma and dairy but never frozen.

5.3. The agent books the dock through Dockwise for Nagpur, Guwahati and
Coimbatore alike. A phone slot at Guwahati is confirmed in Dockwise the next
working day.

5.4. Pharma critical bookings that would need a night segment are passed to
Fleet Control before they are confirmed to the customer, because a night pharma
run needs two named drivers.

5.5. A booking the customer changes after 15:00 the day before is treated as a
new booking.

# PROJ-124: Red sleeve replenishment and passive shipper pilot

**PROJ-124** is open. It has two halves that share a sponsor and a budget line
but nothing else: getting physical red sleeve packets back into every DC, and
piloting validated passive shippers at Nagpur. It is not
[PROJ-123](19-project-PROJ-123-dockwise-rollout.md), which was a dock calendar
project and is closed.

## 10. Emergency cold for a customer's kitchen

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their
own freezer fails. Customer service takes the request; the DC decides whether it
can be done.

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing
can be ready, and the agent passes that on.

10.3. Emergency dry-ice packing is billed at a minimum of 10 kg per request,
whatever smaller quantity the kitchen asks for, and the per-kg price is the one
on the rate card in force.

10.4. Dry ice is never sent in a customer's own car unless the customer's driver
signs the dry-ice safety note at the gate. Customer service sends the note to
the customer with the confirmation.

10.5. Pharma customers are not offered dry-ice packing as an emergency measure.

## Out of scope

PROJ-124 does not change any notification timing, any excursion duration or any
dock grace period. It does not buy shippers for Guwahati or Coimbatore; those
sites continue to refuse pharma staging beyond the SOP limit until a later
project is approved.
