## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

How stock leaves quarantine bays Q-3 (Nagpur), Q-G2 (Guwahati) and Q-C1 (Coimbatore) after QA has recorded a disposition under clause 6.5 of the [Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). ## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

## 4. Return to the customer

4.1. Returned stock travels on return challan QCL-F-33, with the seal number written on it.

4.2. If the stock arrived with a customer logger, the same logger travels back with it.

4.3. A DC manager may arrange the vehicle for a return, but may not sign QCL-F-31.

## 10. Closure

10.1. The QA head or nominated deputy closes pharma critical investigations. The
DC manager may close dairy and frozen investigations only after QA records the
disposition.

10.2. Corrective and preventive actions must have an owner, a due date, and
evidence of completion. "Discussed on call" is not completion evidence.

10.3. Training actions shall be assigned by role, not by name alone, so that new
staff receive the same correction.

10.4. The case file must be kept for seven years for pharma critical stock and
three years for food stock.

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing

restaurant chain whose own freezer has failed, and top-up of a frozen body that

6.2. The dry-ice chest stands in the open-sided store shed beside the wash pad,

Until 2024 the ammonia muster point was M1, the canteen lawn. In the July 2024 monsoon drill the windsock put the canteen lawn downwind of the compressor house for four of the six drill hours.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed temperature
excursion in Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. warehouses, docks, cross-dock
lanes, owned reefer trucks and hired trucks working under Quillfern dispatch.
The procedure applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled dairy, paneer, frozen food,
and any customer stock moved under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. The purpose is to protect patient safety, food safety, customer evidence,
and the company record. A fast release is never preferred over a complete
temperature history. Staff must treat a missing record as a quality event until
QA closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration. A single hand-held thermometer reading is not
enough to release product after a breach; it may be used only to start immediate
containment while the logger history is retrieved.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion is
declared when any approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion is
declared when the approved record is more than +8.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. An insulin low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.3. Milk and paneer must remain from 0.0 C to +4.0 C while in cold rooms and
reefer bodies. A dairy high excursion is declared when milk or paneer is above
+5.0 C for 30 continuous minutes, including staging time after dock release.

2.4. Frozen food must remain at or below -18.0 C. A frozen-food excursion is
declared when the approved record is warmer than -15.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes.

2.5. The Nagpur central hub is also referred to as "NGP hub" in older records.
For this SOP, Nagpur DC and NGP hub mean the same facility unless a customer
contract names a different annex.

2.6. Legacy staging note retained from revision 2.0: milk crates may remain on a
covered dock until +7.0 C for 45 minutes before QA notice is required. This
paragraph has not been relied on since revision 4.0 and is retained only because
customer annex QF-Dairy-11 still quotes it.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Patient-critical stock: notify the customer within 1
hours of a confirmed excursion. Sanjot Bhamra holds the escalation list.

5.2. Food customers are told by the next scheduled check-in unless spoilage is
visible or odour is present.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Paneer must remain between +0.0 C and +5.0 C. A high
excursion is declared when an approved sensor records more than +5.0 C for
45 continuous minutes.

2.2. A low excursion is declared below +0.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. Staging time on a covered dock counts towards both.

2.3. Room CDM-B2 is the paneer room at Bilaspur. Quarantine bay CDM-Q6 receives any
stock placed on hold.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines how Cindermoor Distribution responds to a suspected or confirmed
temperature excursion in its cold rooms, docks, cross-dock lanes and reefer
bodies at the Bilaspur site. It applies to paneer and to any customer stock moved
under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. An excursion means a recorded temperature outside the allowed band for
longer than the allowed duration. One hand-held reading does not release stock.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## 9. Insulated boxes in the load

9.1. A validated passive shipper carries pharma stock inside a reefer body or on
a body without a cradle, such as RF-119.

9.2. A closed shipper is validated for 48 hours from the lid-closing time
written in the shipper register. A shipper that will still be on the road at 40
hours is called in to Fleet Control, and QA decides whether it is re-packed or
the consignment is held.

9.3. The shipper's lid is never opened on the road. The tamper label across the
lid seam is photographed at departure and again at delivery.

9.4. Shippers travel upright, strapped to the body wall, and never under other
freight.

9.5. The empty shipper comes back on the return run in the same condition it
went out, with its packs inside and its logger taped in place, so that QA can
download the logger and count the pack cycles.

## 1. What this manual covers

1.1. The manual covers owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans and escort
cars moving under a Quillfern dispatch note, from the moment a vehicle is taken
over at a DC until it is handed back with its paperwork.

1.2. It does not cover warehouse work inside the cold rooms, customer contracts,
or pricing. A driver who is asked a price by a customer refers the customer to
customer service.

1.3. Revision 3 of July 2026 added section 9 on passive shippers in transit and
moved the police-check rules into section 7.

1.4. Where the manual and the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy seem to
differ, the policy applies. Where the manual and the SOP seem to differ on
anything about temperature, the SOP applies.

1.5. Copies of the manual are kept at the Fleet Control desk in Nagpur, in the
gate cabin at each DC and in the driver rest room at Nagpur. Drivers are not
expected to carry it; the cab card carries what a driver needs on the road.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

## 3. How long stock may sit

3.1. Quarantine Dwell Limit (QDL) is the time stock may stay in quarantine after the excursion is confirmed before the account manager must escalate to the customer's quality head.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| pharma critical | 72 hours |

3.2. Reaching the QDL does not release anything. It starts an escalation; the stock stays where it is.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| dairy | 12 hours |

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| frozen food | 48 hours |

## 1. Release

1.1. Release is recorded on form QCL-F-31 and signed by the QA investigator and a second QA officer who did not investigate the case.

1.2. A white RELEASED tag is fixed beside the red hold tag. The red hold tag is never removed; both stay on the stock until it leaves the site.

1.3. Stock is not released between 22:00 and 06:00, whatever the dispatch plan says. The earliest release of the day is at 06:00.

1.4. Released quantity is counted twice by two people and entered separately from any destroyed quantity.

## 4. Return to the customer

4.1. Returned stock travels on return challan QCL-F-33, with the seal number written on it.

4.2. If the stock arrived with a customer logger, the same logger travels back with it.

4.3. A DC manager may arrange the vehicle for a return, but may not sign QCL-F-31.

## 4. Seal books

4.1. Seals come from the seal manufacturer in books, already numbered in order.
Stores records the first and last number of each book received.

4.2. Stores issues seal books to a DC gate one book at a time against the gate's
signature. Besides the book open at the gate, a gate may hold at most two
unopened books in its locked drawer; a third is not issued until one of the two
is opened.

4.3. Spoiled seals marked VOID come back to Stores with their stubs. Stores
counts the stubs against QCL-F-35 every Friday, and a number that is neither
fitted, spoiled nor on the shelf is reported to Fleet Control the same day.

4.4. Each DC holds two bolt-seal cutters, and a lost cutter is replaced by Stores
within one working day.

4.5. Tamper labels for pharma pallets and shipper lids are issued in rolls of
200 to QA, not to the gate.

4.6. Seal books for Guwahati and Coimbatore go by courier, two books at a time,
and are signed for at the gate cabin on arrival.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## 12. Suppliers

12.1. Stores keeps the approved supplier list for consumables. At the time of
this revision it includes Vidarbha Gases for dry ice at Nagpur, Brahmaputra
Industrial Gases at Guwahati and Kovai Industrial Gases at Coimbatore, Metrosure
Labs for external calibration, and the seal manufacturer named on the current
purchase order.

12.2. A supplier's replacement goods are received like any other delivery. A
supplier who replaces a batch of faulty seals sends new numbers; Stores never
accepts replacement seals carrying the same numbers as the faulty ones.

12.3. Suppliers are reviewed each year on short deliveries, damaged goods and
late replacement. The review is held with Finance and the DC managers.

12.4. A supplier whose driver has to wait more than an hour at the Nagpur store
is told why, and the wait is noted, because suppliers remember waits when they
quote.

## 2. The Stores team and hours

2.1. The Nagpur store is run by Nalini Patil with two storekeepers on the day
shift. It is open from 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Saturday.

2.2. At night, the night shift lead holds the key to the emergency cupboard,
which carries red sleeve packets, seal books and protective equipment only.
Anything taken from it at night is written on the cupboard sheet and signed for
properly the next morning.

2.3. The Guwahati cage is looked after by the shift lead named by Riniki Bora.
The Coimbatore cage is looked after by the morning shift lead.

2.4. Stores is not a place to wait, eat or charge a phone. Drivers collecting
seal books or sleeves wait at the counter.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written
VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

# Stores and Consumables Standard

How Stores receives, holds and issues the consumables that cold-chain work runs
on: seals, red sleeve packets, spare loggers, gel packs, dry ice, protective
equipment and forms. It covers the main store at Nagpur and the smaller stores
cages at Guwahati and Coimbatore. It does not say how any of these items is used
on the job; the documents that govern their use do that.

## 5. Taking a booking

5.1. A booking needs the product class, the quantity in the unit the rate card
uses, the pickup and delivery points, the earliest and latest delivery time, and
the name of the person who will receive.

5.2. The agent checks that the booked vehicle can carry the product class. RF-120
is frozen only; RF-119 takes pharma only with a passive shipper; RF-118 takes
pharma and dairy but never frozen.

5.3. The agent books the dock through Dockwise for Nagpur, Guwahati and
Coimbatore alike. A phone slot at Guwahati is confirmed in Dockwise the next
working day.

5.4. Pharma critical bookings that would need a night segment are passed to
Fleet Control before they are confirmed to the customer, because a night pharma
run needs two named drivers.

5.5. A booking the customer changes after 15:00 the day before is treated as a
new booking.

## 8. Claims

8.1. A customer claim for damaged or lost stock is accepted in writing only,
from a named contact on the account.

8.2. A claim is registered only when it arrives within 30 days of delivery and
carries photographs of the stock and the seal taken at delivery.

8.3. The agent registers the claim, acknowledges it within one working day, and
passes it to the account manager. The agent does not give an opinion on it.

8.4. Stock value in a claim is taken from the Finance schedule. A value in the
customer's email is recorded as the declared value and nothing more.

8.5. A claim that turns on a temperature record waits for QA's investigation.
The customer is told it is waiting, and given the investigation's reference.

8.6. Claims for trips before 18 August 2025 quote the KLP trip number, not a TSL
one.

## 10. Emergency cold for a customer's kitchen

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their
own freezer fails. Customer service takes the request; the DC decides whether it
can be done.

10.2. The agent does not promise a time. The DC tells the agent when the packing
can be ready, and the agent passes that on.

10.3. Emergency dry-ice packing is billed at a minimum of 10 kg per request,
whatever smaller quantity the kitchen asks for, and the per-kg price is the one
on the rate card in force.

10.4. Dry ice is never sent in a customer's own car unless the customer's driver
signs the dry-ice safety note at the gate. Customer service sends the note to
the customer with the confirmation.

10.5. Pharma customers are not offered dry-ice packing as an emergency measure.

# Ammonia alarm at Nagpur: why M2, and why nobody goes back

## Why M2 and not the canteen lawn

Until 2024 the ammonia muster point was M1, the canteen lawn. In the July 2024 monsoon drill the windsock put the canteen lawn downwind of the compressor house for four of the six drill hours.
M2, by gate 2, sits upwind under the south-west monsoon wind and has a second
way out on to the ring road. M1 is still the fire muster point.

## Places

- **M1** — canteen lawn; fire muster only.
- **M2** — beside the windsock at gate 2; ammonia and fire muster.
- **windsocks** — one on the compressor house roof, one at gate 2.

# Ammonia plant at Nagpur: levels, places and kit

## Alarm levels

- about 5 ppm — the smell is noticeable; not an alarm.
- Stage 1 — 25 ppm at any plant-room detector: amber beacon, the plant crew investigate, and dock 5 stops loading.
- Stage 2 — 150 ppm at any detector: site siren and full evacuation to M2.
- 300 ppm — immediately dangerous to life or health; nobody without a breathing set is anywhere near it.

# Ammonia alarm card, canteen notice board

## When the site siren sounds

1. Stop forklifts and trucks, engines off. Do not drive through the plant yard.
2. Leave by the nearest door away from the compressor house.
3. Go to muster point M2 by gate 2, beside the windsock.
4. The shift lead counts heads against the gate register within 15 minutes and rings the plant operator on extension 251 with the count.
5. Nobody goes back for stock, phones or trucks.

## What was done

- Kalpa platform access ended on **30 April 2026**, the date the 2026 decision
  record set for retiring the export script.
- Trip data from 2014 to 2025 was exported to cold storage: 48,900 trips, all
  carrying the KLP prefix, 2.1 TB including the raw probe series. Two copies,
  one on the Pune HQ archive volume and one with the audit vendor.
- The alert routing that Kalpa used was retired with it. What it looked like is
  described in [the Kalpa Alert Routing Guide](archive/a02-kalpa-alert-routing-guide-2021.md),
  which is kept only so auditors can see how alarms were routed before
  Compliance-Red existed.
- The guard cabin tablet at Nagpur was wiped of its login and left in place as a
  read-only audit device. It must not be used to open or acknowledge an alarm.
- The Kalpa sticker on the Nagpur admin wall was removed on 5 May 2026. The
  night team had asked for this twice because new drivers were reading it as
  current.

## Consequences

The decision should be reviewed no earlier than April 2026 unless three major
alert failures occur in a single quarter. A major alert failure means patient
critical stock, no automatic alert to Fleet Control or QA, and a confirmed
temperature breach.

IT must maintain an export script for Kalpa reports. QA must note that Kalpa
uses five-minute polling and may require interpolation in timelines. Fleet must
continue keeping paper driver call logs because Kalpa's door-open event is not
trusted during poor network coverage.

Col. Sandhu's closing comment: "We will not chase a fashionable dashboard while
our drivers and auditors know the present one. STABILITY FIRST; NOVELTY SECOND."

## Reasons

Kalpa has local service staff within Nagpur city limits and has historically
replaced failed truck devices within one working day. The Nagpur base station is
already mounted and wired. Driver training material, customer report templates,
and the QA audit binder already use Kalpa screenshots. Switching all material
before vaccine season would create training risk.

The Kalpa quote is lower than Tessaline's first commercial quote. Tessaline
quoted Rs. 31.20 lakh for migration, device replacement, and API onboarding.
Tessaline also proposed 60-second polling and a richer API, but the API was not
available for our trial vehicles. Kalpa's five-minute polling is not ideal, but
it is known and accepted by current customer annexes.

The exit clause for Kalpa is acceptable only at contract end. Leaving early
would require six months of minimum recurring charges. This is not justified on
the evidence available in November 2023.

## ⚠ One row this review did not update

**The customer notification row above is deliberately blank.** At the time of
this review two customer notification matrices were on file and the reviewer
could not confirm which one Customer Service had been issued. Do not guess from
this map: open the matrices themselves, take the one with the later effective
date, and check whether it amends the SOP clause rather than merely repeating
it. This row will be filled at the next review of this map.

# PROJ-125: Kalpa decommission and audit export

**PROJ-125** ended Quillfern's use of Kalpa Fleet Systems as a running platform
and preserved its history as files. It is closed. PROJ-125 is the last of the
three projects in this series; the other two are
[PROJ-123](19-project-PROJ-123-dockwise-rollout.md) and
[PROJ-124](20-project-PROJ-124-red-sleeve-and-passive-shippers.md), and neither
of them touched a telematics platform.

## Documents kept for history only

These are in the archive. They are evidence of what a rule used to be, and they
are not a rule now.

- [Temperature Excursion Response SOP revision 2.0](archive/a01-sop-temperature-excursion-rev2.md)
- [Kalpa Alert Routing Guide](archive/a02-kalpa-alert-routing-guide-2021.md)
- [Dock scheduling wiki page, 2021](archive/a03-dock-scheduling-wiki-2021.html)
- [Driver Hours and Road Discipline Policy, 2019](archive/a04-driver-hours-policy-2019.md)
- [new joiner induction checklist, 2020](archive/a05-induction-checklist-2020.txt)

The exported dock wiki page,
[09-dock-scheduling-wiki-export.html](09-dock-scheduling-wiki-export.html), is
not in the archive folder but it is not the booking rule either; it was replaced
by the 2026 rules. The same is true of
[the 2024 rate card](07-rate-card-and-surcharges.md).

## Decision

Quillfern will renew Kalpa Fleet Systems for 36 months beginning 1 January 2024.
The renewal covers 147 owned reefers, 63 hired-truck devices during peak months,
and 38 fixed sensors across rooms and docks. The implementation and renewal
charge is Rs. 18.40 lakh. The recurring charge is Rs. 920 per active truck per
month and Rs. 310 per fixed sensor per month.

No split-vendor model will be used in 2024. IT will keep one support desk and
one monthly export from Kalpa. Fleet and QA will continue to use the KLP trip
number for audit packets.

## Scope

The vendor change itself was not this project. It was decided in the cutover
thread of 2025 and recorded afterwards in
[Telematics Vendor Decision 2026](11-decision-telematics-vendor-2026.md), which
retired [the 2023 decision](05-decision-telematics-vendor-2023.md). PROJ-125 only
did the shutdown work that decision left behind.

## At the destination

6. Receiver reads the number before cutting. Mismatch or broken seal: photograph it and call the QA desk on extension 440 before the doors open.
7. Cut seals stay in the trip bag for 7 days.

## 7. When the doors are opened on the road

7.1. Police, excise, sales tax and transport officers may stop a loaded reefer
and ask to see the load. Drivers cooperate, and do not argue about cold chain
at the roadside.

7.2. The driver asks for the officer's name and badge number and writes both on
the back of the dispatch note, with the time and place. The driver photographs
the seal before it is cut, if the officer allows.

7.3. After the inspection the driver fits a fresh bolt seal from the road pack
of five kept in the cab locker, writes the new number beside the old one on the
dispatch note, and photographs it. The cut seal goes into the trip bag.

7.4. The driver then phones Fleet Control on extension 301, while parked, and
Fleet Control enters both seal numbers in QCL-F-35 against the trip.

7.5. If the inspection kept the doors open for more than a few minutes on a
pharma critical load, Fleet Control tells QA, and the minutes are part of the
temperature record like any other door opening.

7.6. The receiver at the destination is told in advance by Fleet Control that
the seal was changed on the road, so that the number mismatch is not treated as
a tamper.

## 12. Paperwork that comes back

12.1. Each trip returns a trip bag holding the dispatch note, the fuel slips,
the cut seals, the takeover sheet and any exception form.

12.2. The trip bag is handed to the shift lead at the returning DC, who checks
it against the dispatch note and signs for it.

12.3. A missing item in the trip bag is written on the dispatch note as
missing, never replaced with a guess. A torn fuel slip is kept torn.

12.4. Trip bags from a trip involving a tyre change or other vendor work carry
the vendor's job sheet with the hours and the spare parts used, so that Fleet
Control can match it to the vendor's invoice.

12.5. Trip bags are kept by Fleet Control for three years, or seven where the
trip involved a pharma critical excursion, a crash, an insurance claim or a
police matter.

## 11. Canteen, lockers and shifts

11.1. The canteen opens at 05:30 and closes at 22:30. The contractor serves
breakfast, a lunch thali and evening tiffin. Drivers waiting for a slot may use
the canteen but not the lockers.

11.2. Lockers are in the annexe ground floor. Each employee has one locker and
one key. Night-shift lockers are opened with the spare key held by security,
signed out in the key register at the gate cabin.

11.3. Shift changes are at 06:00 and 14:00. The outgoing shift lead walks the
cold block with the incoming one and hands over the Dockwise day list, the
quarantine list and any open alarm.

11.4. Overtime is approved by the DC manager in advance. Staff do not stay on
past 22:00 to finish a load; the load waits for the morning shift.

11.5. The first-aid box is in the canteen, and a second box is in the gate
cabin. The nearest hospital with a casualty department is 6 km away on the
Avinashi Road.

# Seal handling card, gate cabin

Kept on the gate cabin counter beside the seal register.

## Fitting

1. Next seal in number order from the open book. Never skip a number.
2. Owned reefer: bolt seal on the rear door hasp. Hired truck: cable seal.
3. Seal number on the dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.
4. Photograph the seal with the dock clock in frame.
5. Spoiled while fitting: cut it, bag it with the stub, write VOID in QCL-F-35 and return it to Stores within 72 hours.

## 13. Language and new people

13.1. Coimbatore works in Tamil. Training is given by a trainer in Tamil, with
English slides available but never used instead of a trainer.

13.2. New joiners spend their first week on the morning shift only. They are not
put on the late shift, and never left alone in the cold block, until a shift
lead has signed them off.

13.3. Every new joiner is shown the gate cabin, the security roster and the key
register on the first day. They are told that security will not open anything
for them at night except in an emergency, and that the lockers, the cabinet and
the seal drawer are all separate keys.

13.4. New drivers from hired-truck vendors are shown the south gate routine by
the guard and the Temple Street timing by the shift lead before their first
booking.

13.5. The words used on site follow the company glossary. A new joiner who hears
a word they do not know is expected to ask, on any shift, and nobody at
Coimbatore is to laugh at the question.

## 5. Diesel, cards and the reefer tank

5.1. Every owned reefer carries one fuel card for the truck and one for the
reefer unit, in separate sleeves. The two are billed to different cost centres
and must not be swapped.

otherwise the driver's judgement, with the rule that no vehicle is allowed to
run so low that it must stop somewhere unlit.

5.5. Fuel slips are photographed at the pump and the photograph is sent to
Fleet Control while parked. The paper slip goes into the trip bag.

5.6. A card that is refused at a listed pump is reported to Fleet Control, and
the driver waits for Fleet Control to authorise a payment. Drivers do not pay
for diesel from their own money.

10.1. Restaurant chains sometimes ask for emergency dry-ice packing when their

## 13. Records

13.1. Tickets, emails, call notes and quotations are kept in the customer

13.2. The agent writes what the customer said and what the agent said, not a

7.1. When QA confirms an excursion, customer service sends the first notice.

because the windows have changed and may change again.

7.2. The first notice uses only the wording the matrix fixes. It promises

7.3. A pharma critical notice is signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.

7.4. The agent records every call and email to the customer in QCL-F-17,

7.5. After QA records a disposition, the second notice names it in the matrix's

agent says that the account manager will reply, and passes the question on.

7.6. Numbers in a notice are kept apart: the quantity affected, the quantity
destroyed and the quantity released are separate lines. The March 2025 vaccine

## 15. Visitors and audits

15.1. Every visitor signs the visitor book at the gate cabin and wears a visitor
badge for the whole visit. A visitor who has not signed in is not shown round,

15.2. Customer auditors are escorted by the DC manager or a shift lead from the

15.3. Photographs inside the cold block are taken only with the DC manager's
permission, and only of the thing being audited. A customer's stock is never

15.4. Auditors from the landlord's insurer visit once a year. They look at the
building, the fire equipment and the roof units, not at the cold chain. The DC

15.5. After any audit the DC manager writes a short note of what was asked,
what was shown and what was promised, and sends it to Revathi Iyer and Farhan

in anyone's memory.

15.6. School and college groups are not shown round the cold block. Requests

8.2. Rain cover over rear pallets is used at Coimbatore from October to December

8.5. The cold block wall sweats in the monsoon. Anything stored against it on
the dry side is moved 30 cm away from the wall from October onwards.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## 3. How long stock may sit

3.1. Quarantine Dwell Limit (QDL) is the time stock may stay in quarantine after the excursion is confirmed before the account manager must escalate to the customer's quality head.

| product class | QDL |

| pharma critical | 72 hours |

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| dairy | 12 hours |

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| frozen food | 48 hours |

3.2. Reaching the QDL does not release anything. It starts an escalation; the stock stays where it is.

## 6. After the washdown

6.1. A washed body is not loaded until it has been chilled again from empty; the dispatch checklist for the load sets how long.

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 2. Conditional release of pharma stock

2.1. Before a conditional release QA calculates the Stability Budget Remaining (SBR): the minutes above +8.0 C that the customer's stability letter allows for the lot, minus the minutes already used in this and every earlier excursion on the same lot.

2.2. A lot with an SBR below 30 minutes is not conditionally released. It is held pending external decision.

2.3. The SBR and the letter reference are written on QCL-F-31.

# Ammonia plant at Nagpur: levels, places and kit

## Alarm levels

- about 5 ppm — the smell is noticeable; not an alarm.
- Stage 1 — 25 ppm at any plant-room detector: amber beacon, the plant crew investigate, and dock 5 stops loading.
- Stage 2 — 150 ppm at any detector: site siren and full evacuation to M2.
- 300 ppm — immediately dangerous to life or health; nobody without a breathing set is anywhere near it.

# Dry ice: properties and limits

## What it is

- **dry ice** — solid carbon dioxide. At normal pressure it turns straight into gas at -78.5 C; it does not melt into a liquid.
- **pellet** — the 16 mm form Quillfern buys from Vidarbha Gases.
- **sublimation loss** — stock that turns to gas while waiting; about 8% of the chest's contents a day with the lid shut.

## Taking it out

1. Sign the pellets out on QCL-F-26 with the kg, the job and your name.
2. Scoop the pellets into an insulated tote. Never put dry ice in a sealed box, a flask or a drum with a screw lid.
3. A load above 10 kg is carried by two people.
4. Dry ice never travels in a driver's cab, and never goes into cold room C2 or C3.

## Before loading

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## 4. Conditions

4.2. Every run carries one validated passive shipper as backup, hired per trip. Its gel packs must have completed their Shipper Conditioning Time (SCT) of 18 hours at +5.0 C before the run is booked.

4.3. A USB logger travels in the load compartment on every run. The tunnel gap is written as missing, never filled.

4.4. Departure checks for this lane are on [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md).

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## 3. Getting a vehicle in and out

3.1. Reefers use the south gate. The east gate is for dry grocery only unless
the DC manager approves an emergency move, as the old wiki page also said.

3.2. School traffic on Temple Street blocks the turn into the south gate between
07:45 and 08:30. Drivers are told on booking to arrive either before 07:30 or
after 08:40. A reefer is never queued across Temple Street; if the apron is
full, the driver goes round the block and comes back.

3.3. Security holds each vehicle outside the south gate until the previous one
has cleared the apron. The apron takes one reefer and one van at a time, no
more, because a reversing reefer cannot see a second one parked behind it.

3.4. Bookings are made in Dockwise, which Coimbatore joined on 1 February 2026.
The grace table and the cancellation rule are the company rule, not a local
one, and are not repeated here.

3.5. Frozen loads are placed before lunch. After about 13:00 the afternoon sun
lies across the outer apron, drivers open their doors to check paperwork, and
the frozen body loses cold it cannot spare.

3.6. Reversing on the apron after dark needs a spotter with a torch, whatever
the vehicle's camera shows. The apron lights are on a timer that the landlord
controls, and they have twice failed to come on in the monsoon.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

## 1. What Stores does

1.1. Stores buys nothing on its own authority. It raises a request against a
purchase order that Finance has approved, receives the goods, holds them, issues
them against a signature and counts them.

1.2. The Nagpur main store keeps the stock for Nagpur and sends stock to
Guwahati and Coimbatore by courier or on a scheduled vehicle. The Guwahati and
Coimbatore cages hold only what their DC uses in about a month.

1.3. Every item issued is signed for by the person who takes it. An item that
leaves Stores without a signature is counted as lost at the next count.

1.4. Stores does not lend. An item taken for a job is either used, returned or
written off, and each of those is recorded.

## 10. Seal books and the security cabin

10.1. Seal books for Coimbatore are issued by Stores at Nagpur and arrive by
courier two books at a time. They are kept in the locked drawer in the gate
cabin, not in the office annexe, because the gate cabin is staffed all night and
the annexe is not.

10.2. Only one seal book is open at the gate at a time. The guard hands a seal
to the shift lead; the guard never fits a seal himself.

10.3. The rest of the sealing rule is the company rule. Seal numbers go on the
dispatch note and in QCL-F-35 before the vehicle moves.

10.4. A vehicle arriving with a broken seal or a number that does not match is
kept outside the south gate, photographed, and reported to Fleet Control before
anyone opens the doors.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

## 13. Forms and printed stationery

13.1. Stores holds the printed pads of every QCL form used on the floor, from the
customer intimation form to the wash register. Each pad carries the form number
and the revision printed at its foot.

13.2. When QA issues a new revision of a form, Stores withdraws every pad of the
earlier revision from the DC shelves in the same week and sends the withdrawn
pads to QA to be counted and shredded. Two revisions of one form are never on a
shelf at the same time.

13.3. Forms are issued to shift leads by the pad, never by the loose sheet, so
that a used pad can be matched to the shift that used it.

13.4. Stores reorders a form when its stock falls to three months' use. The
print order goes through Finance like any other purchase.

13.5. Dispatch notes are printed with running numbers. Stores records the first
and last number of each box issued to a gate, as it does for other numbered
stock.

## What was turned down

A boiling-point check was rejected: at Nagpur's height water boils below 100 C, and a kettle on a night bench is a scald waiting to happen.
Self-checking probes at Rs. 18,000 each were rejected on cost. Sending probes to
the lab every month was rejected because it doubled the time probes spent away.

Agreed by Revathi Iyer and Anjali Deshmukh on 3 August 2025.

## Hand-held probes

1. Fill the insulated jug with crushed ice made from potable water. Top it up with cold potable water to just below the ice line and stir for 30 seconds.
2. Hold the probe tip 5 cm deep in the slurry, clear of the jug wall, for 3 minutes before you read the display.
3. The probe passes if it reads within 0.5 C of 0.0 C.
4. Repeat for every hand-held probe on the monthly list. A probe is due every 30 days.

## 3. Swab check

3.1. Three swabs: floor front, floor rear, door gasket.

3.2. Each must read 150 or below on the handheld luminometer. One failed swab means the whole washdown is repeated, not just the failed spot.

## What was chosen

A monthly ice-point check at the Nagpur QA bench, with one external lab
calibration a year kept for traceability. The BharatVac annex QF-Pharma-04 asks
for a traceable certificate on every instrument used as evidence, and quotes
±0.5 C for hand-held instruments; the bench pass band was set to match. USB
loggers are held tighter, at 0.3 C, because in a dispute the logger file is the
evidence and the probe is only the first look.

# Probe calibration: why the ice-point bench

## What we had

Until July 2025 every hand-held probe went to Metrosure Labs, Pune, once a
quarter. Each lab round took the probes away for 9 working days, at Rs. 1,450 per probe per visit.
With 64 probes across three DCs that came to Rs. 3.71 lakh a year, and the
probes were away exactly when the night shifts needed them.

# Probe and logger calibration at the QA bench

Carried out at the QA bench in Nagpur by any QA officer or trained shift lead.
The bench kit is the insulated jug, the ice scoop, the calibration chamber and
the bench master logger.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

## USB loggers

5. Put the logger beside the bench master in the calibration chamber at +5.0 C for 30 minutes; it passes if it reads within 0.3 C of the master.
6. Every spare logger is checked this way before it is packed into a red sleeve, whatever its sticker says.

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

## What pushed the change

The March 2025 investigation at Nagpur found a hand-held probe reading 1.1 C
high three weeks after its lab certificate. A quarterly lab visit does not catch
drift that fast.

answer_text:
## Impact

The stock was not released on the morning route. BharatVac provided a stability
letter for part of the consignment after reviewing lot data. QA destroyed
13,200 vials and conditionally released 5,200 vials under BharatVac letter
BV-QA-2025-0312. Finance booked a write-off of Rs. 7.82 lakh for the destroyed
vials, packaging, and reverse logistics.

The customer notification was late. Under the incident practice then in use, we
treated customer notice as a same-day item after QA review. That is not
acceptable for patient critical stock. The revised procedure must require
customer notice within two hours after confirmation.

The incident also consumed most of the night shift's available quarantine space.
Two dairy returns were left in the outer holding lane while Q-3 was cleared for
the vaccine pallets. No dairy spoilage was confirmed, but the congestion made
the response slower and showed that pharma critical quarantine cannot depend on
moving unrelated stock at the last minute.

Customer service received three different numbers during the morning: 18,400
vials affected, 13,200 vials destroyed, and 5,200 vials conditionally released.
All three numbers were true in their own context, but the first customer draft
mixed them together. The final notice separated affected quantity, destroyed
quantity, and released quantity.

## Half one: red sleeves

The red sleeve is the packet clipped to an excursion file or a pharma truck
file. What it must contain is fixed by clause 4.2 of
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md); this
project buys the packets and does not change the contents list.

The trigger was operational, not a policy gap. Stores had been promising vendor
plastic sleeves "next week" since April 2026, and the Nagpur night team recorded
a second short packet on 19 June 2026, writing RED SLEEVE MISSING on a printout
for a BharatVac return — see
[the night shift handover log](04-night-shift-handover-log.txt). The same log
records hired trucks arriving without sleeves in October 2025 and staff making
red tags out of old labels.

Ordered: 60 packets at Rs. 1,180 each, split 30 Nagpur, 15 Guwahati,
15 Coimbatore. Each packet is made up with a spare calibrated logger before it
leaves QA, because a sleeve without a logger is the failure this project is
meant to end.

## 6. Where the truck is

6.1. Customers ask where their vehicle is more than they ask anything else.

6.2. Customer service gives an ETA only from Fleet Control's board, rounded to
30 minutes, and never calls the driver.

6.3. If the board shows no position, because of a dead zone, the agent says that
the vehicle is in an area without signal and gives the last known position and
time. The agent does not guess.

6.4. A customer who has the driver's number and calls him directly is asked, the
next time customer service speaks to them, to call customer service instead.
Drivers answer only when parked.

6.5. A late vehicle is reported to the customer as late as soon as Fleet Control
says it will miss its window. The reason is given in plain words and without
blame.

## 4. Giving a customer a price

4.1. Agents quote from the rate card in force on the day of the quotation, and
write the rate card's effective date on the quotation.

4.2. BharatVac and Manjara Dairy are never quoted from the rate card. Their
prices come from Finance under their annexes.

4.3. Passive shipper hire is quoted only for consignments that start at Nagpur,
because the shippers are at Nagpur. A shipper cannot be quoted on a Guwahati or
Coimbatore dispatch unless the account manager has arranged for the consignment
to go through Nagpur.

4.4. The Guwahati monsoon handling line is quoted only on Guwahati loads in its
months. It is not added to Coimbatore or Nagpur loads.

4.5. The diesel surcharge is quoted as a rule, not as a figure: the agent writes
the rule from the rate card and lets the invoice apply it on the day of travel.

4.6. Agents do not discount. Any price below the rate card is an account
manager's call, confirmed in writing by Finance.

## 16. Month-end reporting

16.1. On the third working day of each month, the customer service lead sends
Finance and the account managers a report of the month's tickets by account:
bookings, late vehicles, complaints, credit notes raised and notices sent.

16.2. Each account manager reviews the report for their accounts and writes one
line per account on anything unusual. The lines are sent back to the lead within
two working days.

16.3. The report is not sent to customers as it stands. A customer who wants a
monthly service report gets one written for them by the account manager, from
the same figures.

16.4. Figures in the report come from the customer service system. An agent who
knows a figure is wrong corrects the ticket, not the report.

16.5. The BharatVac and Manjara Dairy accounts get a quarterly review meeting in
addition to the month-end report, held by their account managers with Finance
and QA.

## Summary

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of
rotavirus vaccine in lots ROTA-9A and ROTA-9B. The approved record showed the
room above +8.0 C for 66 minutes. At the time of the event, the SOP required a
QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 11:30 | Customer notice was sent to BharatVac quality contact. |

## Out of scope

PROJ-124 does not change any notification timing, any excursion duration or any
dock grace period. It does not buy shippers for Guwahati or Coimbatore; those
sites continue to refuse pharma staging beyond the SOP limit until a later
project is approved.

answer_text:
## Why pellets

Quillfern used to buy dry ice in blocks. Blocks had to be broken with a mallet on the dock, and two hand injuries in 2024 came from exactly that.
The blocks came in 12 kg slabs, and staff carried the slabs by hand because no
tote was used for them. The chest lid has two handles. Vidarbha Gases rated
pellets as easier to meter by the kg, and pellets of 16 mm from Vidarbha Gases
replaced blocks in 2024.

## Why a second pair of hands

The tote handles are rated for 12 kg, so one person with a full tote is already at the limit of the handles.
A dropped tote on a wet dock scatters pellets that people then pick up with the
wrong gloves.

## Alarm levels

- about 5 ppm — the smell is noticeable; not an alarm.
- Stage 1 — 25 ppm at any plant-room detector: amber beacon, the plant crew investigate, and dock 5 stops loading.

## What RF-119 may carry

RF-119 runs the Guwahati dairy and chilled-grocery circuit. Milk and paneer are
its normal load.

RF-119 may carry vaccines or insulin **only** inside a validated passive
shipper, because the body has no cradle and no second compartment to separate
pharma from dairy stock. A passive shipper is hired per trip and the charge is a
line on [the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md); Fleet Control raises
the hire request, not the customer service agent. Without a shipper, RF-119 is
refused for pharma critical stock whatever the urgency, and
[the Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md)
clause 1.3 is the reason no manager may overrule that at the gate.

The temperature limits for whatever RF-119 carries are set by
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). This
file sets none.

## Monsoon working

RF-119 works Guwahati through the monsoon. Rain cover over rear pallets is
mandatory during monsoon unloading, and since June 2026 the handling is billed
to the customer as a line on [the rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md) rather
than absorbed. The yard rule about not idling inside the small yard after 21:30
is in [Dock scheduling rules 2026](13-dock-scheduling-rules-2026.md).

On 18 April 2026 RF-119 reached Guwahati without a rain cover over the rear
pallets and the night team reported it to Riniki Bora by phone. No stock was
lost. Stores now keeps two spare covers in the RF-119 cab locker.

## Half two: passive shippers

Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock beyond a short limit unless a
validated passive shipper is used; the limit and the exception are clause 8.2 of
[the SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md).

Quillfern has been refusing bookings it could have taken, including chilled
pharma on [RF-119](17-reefer-RF-119-asset-file.md), which has no shipper cradle
and therefore cannot take pharma critical stock without one. The pilot puts
twelve validated passive shippers at Nagpur from August 2026.

Hire is charged to the customer per shipper per trip at the rate printed on
[the H2 2026 rate card](12-rate-card-2026-h2.md). Finance added that line to the
card when this project was approved, so the card and the project were signed in
the same week.

in the same 2021 batch as [RF-118](16-reefer-RF-118-asset-file.md) but it is a
smaller single-compartment body and it is not a pharma asset. Fleet Control has
twice received a Nagpur pharma booking on RF-119 that was meant for RF-118, so
the two files are kept separate and neither one is a copy of the other.

## 10. Hired trucks and their drivers

10.1. A hired-truck vendor is on the approved list before the first booking, and
each of its drivers signs the policy acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

10.2. Hired trucks carry their own fuel. Quillfern fuel cards are never given to
hired drivers.

10.3. Hired trucks are sealed with cable seals. Their drivers are shown the seal
routine at the gate by the shift lead.

10.4. A hired truck without a working temperature display is not loaded with
cold-chain stock, whatever the vendor promises about a repair on the way.

10.5. Vendors are reviewed every quarter on arrival times, refused loads,
exceptions and any safety concern raised by a DC.

## Why cable seals on hired trucks

Hired trucks arrive with every kind of hasp, and a bolt seal does not fit half
of them. A cable seal fits any hasp.

## 16. Tolls and road charges

16.1. Every owned reefer carries an electronic toll tag registered to Quillfern.
The tag balance is topped up by Fleet Control; drivers never pay a toll in cash
unless the tag reader at the plaza has failed.

16.2. A cash toll is paid only against a printed receipt, which goes into the
trip bag. A handwritten receipt is accepted only when the plaza staff sign and
stamp it.

16.3. A tag that shows a low balance at a plaza is reported to Fleet Control
while parked, and Fleet Control tops it up before the next plaza.

16.4. Hired trucks use their own tags. Quillfern does not refund a hired truck's
tolls unless the purchase order says so.

16.5. Road charges at state borders and permit fees are paid by Fleet Control in
advance for owned reefers. A driver asked for money at a border that was not on
the dispatch note calls Fleet Control before paying anything.

## 5. Diesel, cards and the reefer tank

5.1. Every owned reefer carries one fuel card for the truck and one for the
reefer unit, in separate sleeves. The two are billed to different cost centres
and must not be swapped.

5.2. Drivers fill only at Quillfern-listed pumps. The list is printed on the
back of the cab card and updated each quarter by Fleet Control.

5.3. A reefer unit whose fuel falls below one quarter is filled at the next
listed pump before any other stop, including a customer drop.

5.4. The truck's own tank follows the dispatch checklist at departure and is
otherwise the driver's judgement, with the rule that no vehicle is allowed to
run so low that it must stop somewhere unlit.

5.5. Fuel slips are photographed at the pump and the photograph is sent to
Fleet Control while parked. The paper slip goes into the trip bag.

5.6. A card that is refused at a listed pump is reported to Fleet Control, and
the driver waits for Fleet Control to authorise a payment. Drivers do not pay
for diesel from their own money.

# Fleet Operations Manual

The working manual for Fleet Control, fleet planners, owned-reefer drivers and
the managers of hired-truck vendors. It says how the fleet is run day to day. It
does not restate the driver hours limits, the temperature limits or the dock
booking rules; those have their own documents, and this manual points to them.

# Seals: why bolt seals, number order and pallet labels

## Why bolt seals on owned reefers

In 2024 a plastic seal on a Mangal Foods load was cut and replaced with a look-alike carrying the same number, and the shortage claim could not be defended.
A bolt seal needs a cutter to remove and cannot be pushed back together. A bolt seal costs Rs. 38 against Rs. 9 for the plastic seal it replaced.

## What the numbers cost

Plastic seals were bought in bags of 500. The Mangal Foods claim was worth
Rs. 2.6 lakh. Bolt seals are bought through Stores and booked to the Fleet cost
centre. The cutter for bolt seals costs more than a year of plastic seals, and
each DC has two.

## 2. Speed

2.1. The maximum permitted speed for a loaded Quillfern reefer is 65 km/h on
open highway, 55 km/h in rain or fog, and 40 km/h on ghat roads.

## 4. Speed and conduct

4.1. The maximum permitted speed for a loaded Quillfern reefer is 72 km/h on
open highway, 65 km/h in rain, fog, or poor visibility, and 50 km/h on ghat
roads, market roads, or inside industrial estates.

4.2. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited except through a hands-free
device for Fleet Control calls. Messaging, app troubleshooting, and customer
calls must be handled while parked.

4.3. Alcohol, intoxicants, and sedating medicines not declared to Fleet Control
are prohibited. The limit is zero during duty and for eight hours before duty.

4.4. Seat belts are mandatory for driver and passenger. A route assistant who
travels without a belt must be reported as a safety non-conformance, not treated
as a local habit.

4.5. Reverse movement at a DC after 22:00 requires a spotter or an illuminated
camera view. If lighting fails, movement stops until safe guidance is available.

## 1. Scope

1.1. The policy applies to owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans, escort
cars used for pharma critical movement, and any vehicle carrying Quillfern staff
between a DC, customer site, toll plaza, hotel, or repair yard.

1.2. A driver is on duty from the first required report at gate, yard, hotel, or
customer premises until the vehicle is parked, keys are handed over or secured,
documents are deposited, and the driver is released by Fleet Control.

1.3. A customer request, delayed dock slot, vaccine urgency, milk spoilage risk,
or senior manager's impatience does not cancel this policy. NO LOAD IS WORTH A
LIFE.

## 1. Scope

1.1. Empty-room run for 24 hours, then loaded-room run for 48 hours with 18 pallets of water-filled dummy cartons in the vaccine positions. The loaded run replayed the busiest night shift of February 2026, a DOM of 96, with every opening repeated on the same timetable.

1.2. Acceptance: every probe inside +2.0 C to +8.0 C for the whole run, and the room back inside limits within 15 minutes of a 3-minute opening.

## 4. Conclusion

4.1. C2 passed.

4.2. The rack A top-level restriction set in TMS-41 is lifted; the air curtain holds that position.

4.3. From April to September the top level of rack D carries only empty totes and outer packaging, never vaccine.

4.4. The permanent room probe TSL-NGP-C2-07 moves from B2-mid to the WCP.

## 5. Telematics and alerts

5.1. Drivers are not responsible for repairing telematics devices while moving.
If a Tessaline or Kalpa device alarms, the driver shall acknowledge only when
parked or when a co-driver can safely handle the call.

5.2. Fleet Control shall not ask a driver to restart an app, photograph a
dashboard, or read a temperature display while the vehicle is moving.

5.3. Harsh braking, overspeed, door-open, and route deviation alerts must be
reviewed by Fleet within two working days. A coaching call is not punishment;
it is evidence that we noticed the risk.

5.4. A temperature alarm must never be treated as permission to drive faster.
Fleet Control shall first ask whether the driver is safe, parked, or able to
reach a safe stopping point. Product-protection instructions come after the
driver's immediate road safety is confirmed.

5.5. If a customer asks the driver directly for location, temperature, or arrival
time, the driver may answer only while parked. Customer-support staff shall not
forward customer pressure to the driver as a driving instruction. The proper
channel is Fleet Control.

5.6. Telematics coaching records are confidential HR and Fleet records. They may
be used in accident investigation, insurance defence, and safety audit, but they
must not be posted in open operations chat groups for ridicule.

## 7. When stock goes out of range

7.1. When QA confirms an excursion, customer service sends the first notice.
The window, the channel and the signatory are those of the customer notification
matrix with the later effective date. The agent opens the matrix every time,
because the windows have changed and may change again.

7.2. The first notice uses only the wording the matrix fixes. It promises
nothing about release, replacement, credit or insurance.

7.3. A pharma critical notice is signed by the QA head or the nominated deputy.
The agent prepares it; the agent does not sign it.

7.4. The agent records every call and email to the customer in QCL-F-17,
including calls nobody answered.

7.5. After QA records a disposition, the second notice names it in the matrix's
words. If the customer asks what the disposition means for their invoice, the
agent says that the account manager will reply, and passes the question on.

7.6. Numbers in a notice are kept apart: the quantity affected, the quantity
destroyed and the quantity released are separate lines. The March 2025 vaccine
event showed what happens when one draft mixes them.

## 12. Scrap, waste and returns

12.1. Cardboard, stretch wrap and broken pallets are separated at the back of
the south block. A scrap dealer from Kovaipudur collects cardboard and wrap
every Tuesday and pays by the kg.

12.2. Broken pallets are stacked by the east wall for the pallet repairer, who
comes on the first working day of each month.

12.3. The old chest freezer from the closed dairy room still stands by the
scrap pile. It is not used for anything and it is not to be sold until Finance
writes it off.

12.4. Customer returns are received at dock 2 and checked against the return
challan. Frozen returns go into CBE-FROZEN only after the shift lead has
checked the logger with the Nagpur QA desk on the phone.

12.5. Spoiled stock is not scrap. It follows the spoilage and destruction rules
of the SOP, and it is never given to the scrap dealer, whatever its weight.

## 11. Canteen, lockers and shifts

11.1. The canteen opens at 05:30 and closes at 22:30. The contractor serves
breakfast, a lunch thali and evening tiffin. Drivers waiting for a slot may use
the canteen but not the lockers.

11.2. Lockers are in the annexe ground floor. Each employee has one locker and
one key. Night-shift lockers are opened with the spare key held by security,
signed out in the key register at the gate cabin.

11.3. Shift changes are at 06:00 and 14:00. The outgoing shift lead walks the
cold block with the incoming one and hands over the Dockwise day list, the
quarantine list and any open alarm.

11.4. Overtime is approved by the DC manager in advance. Staff do not stay on
past 22:00 to finish a load; the load waits for the morning shift.

11.5. The first-aid box is in the canteen, and a second box is in the gate
cabin. The nearest hospital with a casualty department is 6 km away on the
Avinashi Road.

## 23. Contacts

23.1. The Nagpur store phone is on the Operations extension list. Out of hours,
the night shift lead holds the emergency cupboard key, as in section 2.

23.2. Questions about whether an item is fit to use go to QA. Questions about
whether an item may be bought go to Finance. Stores answers questions about
where an item is and how many are left.

## 6. Where the truck is

6.1. Customers ask where their vehicle is more than they ask anything else.

6.2. Customer service gives an ETA only from Fleet Control's board, rounded to
30 minutes, and never calls the driver.

6.3. If the board shows no position, because of a dead zone, the agent says that
the vehicle is in an area without signal and gives the last known position and
time. The agent does not guess.

6.4. A customer who has the driver's number and calls him directly is asked, the
next time customer service speaks to them, to call customer service instead.
Drivers answer only when parked.

6.5. A late vehicle is reported to the customer as late as soon as Fleet Control
says it will miss its window. The reason is given in plain words and without
blame.

## 19. Office consumables and general supplies

19.1. Stores also holds the everyday supplies the sites run on: printer paper,
toner, pens, markers, stretch wrap, packing tape, pallet labels, torch batteries
for the gate cabins and cleaning materials.

19.2. These are issued against a signature like everything else, but in larger
units: a ream, a box, a roll. Stores does not count pens.

19.3. Stretch wrap and packing tape are issued to the dock teams by the carton at
the start of each week. A dock that runs out before the week ends asks Stores,
and Stores notes which dock and why.

19.4. Pallet labels are printed by the dock teams from Dockwise. Stores holds the
blank label rolls and the spare printer ribbons, and keeps two spare label
printers in the cage for a swap.

19.5. Cleaning materials are issued to the housekeeping contractor against its
own signature. The contractor's staff do not take anything from the cage
themselves.

## 11. Write-off and disposal

11.1. Stores writes off an item only with Finance's approval, recorded on the
write-off sheet.

11.2. Broken instruments are written off after QA has confirmed they cannot be
calibrated. Their serials are struck off the instrument list.

11.3. Damaged seal books are never thrown away. Every seal in them is written
VOID and kept with the stubs until the next audit.

11.4. Protective equipment that is worn out is cut before disposal, so that it
cannot be picked out of the bin and worn again.

# Coimbatore DC site handbook

Everything that is particular to Coimbatore DC, in one place. Company-wide rules
still come from their own documents: temperature limits and excursions from
QCL-QA-SOP-17, dock booking from QCL-OPS-DOCK-03, driver hours from the Driver
Hours and Road Safety Policy. Where this handbook and a company-wide rule seem
to differ, ask the DC manager before acting, and do not assume the handbook
wins. What follows is how those rules are carried out on this site, with this
building, these people and this weather.

## 22. Energy and waste in the store

22.1. The store lights are on a timer and go off at 19:30. The storekeeper
closing the store checks that the cage, the flammables cabinet and the emergency
cupboard are locked before the lights go off.

22.2. Packaging from deliveries is flattened and sent to the scrap area on the
day it arrives. The store is not a place to keep empty boxes.

22.3. Used toner cartridges are returned to the toner supplier for recycling.

22.4. Stores reports its waste once a year to the Nagpur DC manager, by type and
weight, for the site's environmental return.
